text: After they have been dismantled from themachine, cleaned, washed, degreased and dried, the parts are inspected and sorted. The parts are sorted in three groups: fitfor further use without repair, needing repair, and unserviceable. The first group includes parts which have retained their structural or repair dimensions or when the degree of their wear has not exceeded the allowable limits (there are no cracks and other defects and their outward appearance satisfies the specifications). The second group is assigned to parts with modified structural or repair dimensions, having cracks and other defects but which may be repaired. Badly worn, broken, cracked parts which are very difficult to repair and not worth to be restored pertain to the third group. Sorting of parts makes it possible to specify defects in the list which was established prior to the complete disassembly of the m a chine.

text: The serviceable parts are collected in one place, the parts requiring restoring are sent to the shop and unserviceable parts are scrapped to the scrap yard where they are sorted by materials used for their manufacture. To replace the unserviceable parts, the repair team receives new ones from the store. When inspecting and sorting parts, the latter are classified into three groups, i.e. movable important parts, stationary important parts and non-important ones. The parts pertaining to the third group are subjected to outward examination, while the parts of the first two groups are inspected for concealed defects, measured and examined for outward appearance.

text: The sorting inspector must be thoroughly acquainted with the design of machines to be repaired, the conditions of their operation and the technological process of the repair to be carried out. Special instructions and albums of drawings are used for technical inspection of parts. Concealed defects (surface and interior cracks) are uncovered by means of magnetic ultrasonic and luminescent flaw detectors. 68 Chapter Four Magnetic flaw detectors are used for the examination of steel and cast-iron parts. The part is sprayed with a finely dispersed metal powder in suspension in kerosene or transformer oil. When the part is magnetized by the flaw detector, the particles of the powder are disposed according to the power lines of the magnetic flow, while in case of a crack they run along it thus marking itsdisposition and shape.

text: Ultrasonic flaw detectors are based on the capacity of sonic waves with an oscillation frequency of 0.5-10 M H z and higher to propagate in a solid state in the shape of a thin slightly diverging jet. If there is a defect (crack or cavity) in the part it becomes an obstacle for the passage of the ultrasonic wave as the latter is partially reflected and partially dispersed. This testing method allows the detection of defects deeply located in the part.

text: Luminescent flaw detectors u s e t h e c a p a c i t y o f f l u o r e s c e n t s u b s t a n c e s to glow on their irradiation by ultraviolet rays. The part is immersed in bath with fluorescent liquid which penetrates in the finest cracks (if such are present). Further, the part surface is dried and sprayed with silica gel powder, and then irradiated in a chamber with ultraviolet rays. The fluorescent layer remaining in the crack starts glowing and marks out the point and shape of the crack.

Further, the part surface is dried and sprayed with silica gel powder, and then irradiated in a chamber with ultraviolet rays. The fluorescent layer remaining in the crack starts glowing and marks out the point and shape of the crack.

text: Worn-out shafts. The following parts need repairs due to the wear of shafts: journals, surfaces for mounting pulleys, gears and other parts, keyways, threads, etc. The main kinds of repairs of a worn-out shaft are: building-up (hard facing) of the worn-out surface, metal coating or electroplating, placing a ring on the worn plate, or the use of repair sizes in shafts to be repaired. If the wear and crushing of separate shaft elements are very great, new elements are built-up by welding or by a mechanical process in combination with welding. The kind of repairs is a function of the extent of wear, the conditions of shaft operation, the availability of repair facilities Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 71 Fig. 34. Restoring broken shafts by Fig. 35. Repair of worn shafts by building-up •metal coating and of the use of repair dimensions system, as well as economic considerations.

text: In repairing shafts by building-up their worn-out surfaces (journals and necks) must be prepared so that the metal overlay is of about the same thickness. The welding beads are placed in an increasing order (Fig. 34a)or as a spiral (Fig. 34b). This sequence is necessary to prevent shaft warping in building-up. Breaks in the building-up process (for turning the part or cleaning the beads) serve to equalize the welding temperature conditions and to partially protect the part from warping. The crushed or stripped thread is cut off by a cutter and built-up with a big allowance for further machining. In centralized repairs of shafts, the building-up of worn-out places should be carried out automatically on special machines under a layer of flux (see Chapter 2).

text: W h e n the shafts are repaired by metal coating, their surface should be prepared to eliminate the distortions of its geometrical configuration and to increase the surface roughness. O n the surface of the shaft to be metal-coated a rough thread is cut with a pitch of 0.8-1.2 m m and a depth of 0.5-0.8 m m . Then the surface is cleaned from oil stains and dirt by sand blasting. If the journal end is worn out the surface to be metal-plated must be stepped (Fig. 35a) to avoid the loss in journal strength and to retain the pulverized layer. To prevent the end surface from flaking and to strengthen it, safety beads are made by turning or welding (Fig. 35b, c)or also slots may be cut on the surface.

text: In metal coating shafts of intricate shape (crankshafts, shafts with shoulders, flanges, etc.), they are first coated with sprayed metal at places of sharp changes (cranks, ledges, etc.) and then the rest of the surface is sprayed with metal. Metal-coated shafts are machined on lathes as usual. Chromium plating of shafts is carried out as follows: grinding and buffing of the surfaces to be chromium plated; insulating places which are not to be chromium plated, and screening sharp edges and relief points, sand papering; suspending parts from frames, electrolytic degreasing; washing in hot water; etching and chromium plating; washing in running cold water; neutralizing in an alkaline solution; 72 Chapter Four rinsing in hot water; removing the parts from the frame; washing in hot water on nets; inspection; if necessary machining of the chromium-plated surface.

text: When preparing the shafts for ringing, the worn-out journal is turned to obtain a regular shape and the size necessary for appropriate fit. The minimum diameter of the turned place is determined by calculating the strength of the journal. The worn-out journals are fitted with solid rings (couplings) and composite rings are placed on the necks. W h e n necks and journals are passed into the group of parts with repair dimensions they may be restored by turning, or by turning with subsequent grinding, or by grinding only. In case of considerable distortion of the shape, untreated necks and journals are usually turned on a lathe and then ground. When the distortion is inconsiderable, grinding is sufficient. The allowance should be the same as for new shafts. Fig. 36. Centre shifters

text: The aim of machining is to impart the shafts definite shape and dimensions after welding, building-up, metal spraying, chromium plating and also to use the repair dimensions of the part. W h e n choosing conditions for the machining of built-up and metalcoated shafts, it should be taken into account that the hardness of layers is usually higher than that of the parent metal, the surface of coating is not smooth, etc. For this reason, it is necessary to use a lower cutting speed, depth, and a smaller feed as compared with those recommended for working the parent metal.

text: The antifriction and sliding bearings used in textile machines are of most various designs, yet sliding friction bearings only are repaired in textile enterprises. The repair of antifriction bearings is carried out in special bearing repair plants as complicated special equipment is required for this kind of repair. Sliding bearings m a y be classified into solid bearings (with or without bushes) and split bearings (with or without linings). M a n y machines have open bearings (e.g. for fluted rollers of spinning frames).

text: The bearing shells are mainly made of cast iron, while the bushes and linings are made of antifriction cast iron, bronze, zinc and aluminium alloys, metal ceramics (cermet), hard plastics and laminated wood plastics. Also used are bimetallic linings and bushings; cast iron or steel linings and bushings lined with babbitt, bronze, zinc, aluminium and other antifriction alloys. Some bearings (for instance on the shaft of the drawing frame coiler) are cast as a whole with a bracket. The main drawback of sliding bearings is the wear of rubbing surfaces and sometimes their cracks and breakages. Depending on the type, dimensions, materials and kind of defects the bearings are repaired by different methods: metal coating, building-up, pouring with babbitt and bronze, pressing the repair bushings, replacing the worn part, and plastic compression.

text: Metal coating may be used for the repair of bearings of different designs with the exception of long bearers with deep holes of small diameter (for instance spindle tubes and bolsters). When preparing the surface of a bearing or bushing for metal coating, i.e. when eliminating their ovality or conicity by boring and cutting a rough thread, care should be taken that the walls of the workpiece are 74 Chapter Four not excessively weakened. If the bearing is strongly worn-out, the rough thread is to be cut without preliminary boring. Split liningsare prepared for metal coating proceeding as follows. Both halves of a bearing are connected by a clip or soldered together after which they are carefully checked (trued) and secured in a device on the lathe, bored, and rough threaded to a depth of 0.8 mm.

Metal coating may be used for the repair of bearings of different designs with the exception of long bearers with deep holes of small diameter (for instance spindle tubes and bolsters). When preparing the surface of a bearing or bushing for metal coating, i.e. when eliminating their ovality or conicity by boring and cutting a rough thread, care should be taken that the walls of the workpiece are 74 Chapter Four not excessively weakened. If the bearing is strongly worn-out, the rough thread is to be cut without preliminary boring. Split liningsare prepared for metal coating proceeding as follows. Both halves of a bearing are connected by a clip or soldered together after which they are carefully checked (trued) and secured in a device on the lathe, bored, and rough threaded to a depth of 0.8 mm.

text: The split bearings without linings are tightened with bolts and clamped in a four-cam chuck or on the carriage of a turning lathe. The non-split bearings are metal-coated in the same manner. Split linings and bearings are sometimes metal coated in disassembled state manually for obtaining a more uniform metal layer through the use of thickness gauges. Metal-coated bearings are subjected to heat treatment in a reducing m e d i u m at 700-750°C for 2-3 h. This increases the strength of the part and moreover improves the antifriction property and the wearresistance of the part. After metal coating the bearings are bored and reamed and thesplitliningsare complementary scraped. The allow­ ance for machining must be 0.6-0.7 m m at each side.

text: Building-up. If there isno metal coating plant at the enterprise the bearings and linings are repaired by building-up. Building-up ismade with the same materials from which the workpieces have been manufactured. However the antifriction properties of cast-iron linings and bearings are considerably increased by building-up with bronze. The worn surface is prepared for building-up by boring. After the m e ­ chanical treatment, the layer of built-up metal must not be under 1 mm. It is recommended to make longitudinal grooves in dovetail shape on the bearings so that the built-up metal is more reliably retained on the surface.

text: Building-up is done by electric arc or gas welding. Preliminarily the parts are slowly heated: cast-iron linings— to a temperature of 500°C, and bronze linings to 400°C. Building-up is carried out according to a thickness gauge which ensures a greater uniformity of the layer. The allowance for machining is 2-3 mm. After building-up the bronze linings are annealed at a temperature of 500-550°C, then cooled in water. The built-up linings are bored, reamed and scraped. Lining of bearings. Sliding bearings lined with non-ferrous antifriction alloys: babbitt, bronze, zinc and aluminium alloys, polymer materials, etc. find wide application in textile machines.

text: Both new and repaired bearings are lined with bronze owing to which they are imparted higher strength and wear resistance. For this reason, bronze is used for lining heavily loaded bearings. Lining with bronze may be done both manually and by the centrifugal method. Lining with a zinc alloy is usually made on the untinned surface of bearings, while lining with aluminium alloy may be done only when the layer is mechanically attached to the surface of the lined bearing. For this reason it is necessary to provide circular grooves or to cut a thread on the surface of the bearing. Lining may also be made of polymer materials.

text: Repair by mechanical methods and presswork (plastic deformation). Worn-out bearings, linings and bushings are repaired depending on their design either by mechanical methods (by placing inner rings, inserts, and patches) or by presswork (plastic deformation). Heavily worn-out solid bearings are repaired by pressure, placing repair rings (bushings) of antifriction material (cast iron, bronze, aluminium and zinc alloys, fabric-base laminates and other plastic materials).

text: The exterior diameters of the repaired rings depend on the chosen fit and class of accuracy, while the internal diameter ofthe ring (bushing) corresponds to the dimension of the new part or to the next repair dimension. At pressure fitting of rings (bushings) their interior diameter and shape are reduced and for this reason when choosing the interior diameter of the ring it is necessary to take into account the allowance for the final machining in assembly (reaming). Multipillow blocks are subjected to reaming in an assembled and installed state. Sizing may be also done with a ball or punch. Splitted and open bearings without linings are repaired by installing repair semi-rings. In this case the worn-out pillow block is bored and semi-rings or linings of antifriction material are secured on dowels or with glue.

text: Gears may be of cast iron, steel, bronze, fibre-based laminates, capron, leather, etc. They operate at different speeds (from 0.2 to 30 m/min) and transmit different powers. The accuracy of gear manufacture is from coarsely machined to polished ones. The number of gears and toothed quadrants and racks exceeds 100. In the course of operation different kinds of damages occur: wear and breakage of teeth, cracks in the rims and spokes, crushing of butt faces, hubs, walls of key grooves and holes, deterioration of thread in stopping holes. Faulty gears are replaced in couples by new ones at the repairs. If there are no reserve gears available or in urgent cases, the gears should be repaired.

text: Gears with worn-out and broken teeth are repaired by building-up, fitting of tyres or toothed sections and by using cap-screws; and in some cases the gear is turned to the other side to make use of good teeth. Repair of Parts and Assembly Units 79 Fig. 41. Kinds of gear building-up The toothed surface is repaired by overall circular building-up (Fig. 41a), building-up of separate damaged teeth (Fig. 41&-e), and building-up with the formation of tooth contour (Fig. 41f-h). Overall circular building-up as well as building-up of separate teeth are used to repair gears having fine pitch, while welding with formation of teeth contour is employed for repairing gears with a big pitch.

text: Building-up ismade by electric arc and gas welding with preheating (hot building-up) or without it (cold building-up). Hot building-up is usually used for the repair of big gears. If the broken or worn-out teeth are disposed in different places of the gear circumference, building-up should be carried out successively in diametrically opposite places to avoid warping and cracking. Cold building up is employed at the repair of cast-iron gears with small pitch and diameter and especially for the repair of toothed quadrants. W h e n repairing gears with a sufficiently strong rim, several steel pins (cap-screws) with a diameter inferior to the thickness of the tooth are screwed-in in place of the removed tooth.

text: Sometimes if cracked or broken rims of gears, pulleys, and flywheels cannot be replaced by new ones, the worn out parts are repaired by welding the cracks and welding-in the crumbled part of the wheel rim. To eliminate stresses appearing in welding, the part must be slowly cooled. It is also possible to weld cover plates on the inner side of the cracked or broken rim or cover plates and moreover screw couplings may he used for repair (combined method). The best method for repairing the cracks appearing on one or several spokes is by hot or cold welding. In some emergency cases one or two cracked spokes (disposed at different places) may temporarily be tightened together with a clip. For better reliability the cracked spoke must be welded after which a clip is put on. Crushed keyways are filed up or new keyways are cut at some other place and the crushed ends are built-up or cut.

For reducing the contamination of the net with fluff, trash and dust it is coated from inside and outside with spirit varnish so that the cage surface becomes smooth and there is no accumulation of fluff and dirt. text: Rollers and beaters. In blowing scutchers, blade, doffer, cleaning, evening, and spiked rollers are used as well as blade and needle beaters. They are removed from the scutcher and mounted on it by means of a special crane-truck with a hoisting capacity up to 4 kN. The bladerollergets out of order as a result of the deformation and the detachment of separate blades. At repairs the faulty blades are straightened according to the template and loose blades are riveted. Next, the screw space between the blades is checked and the roller is balanced. The dofferrollerconsists of a steel shaft on which six steel rimmed sections are mounted. Between the rims leather blades are clamped which are liable to crack in service.

text: At the repair of doffers, the faulty blades are replaced with new ones made of rubberized belting. The leather or rubberized belt 1 (Fig. 48a) used for making blades must easily bend, but at the same time must be very rigid. Excessively soft blades will bend very qui- Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 89 * ckly and will fail to reach the teeth of the spiked lattice, and on the contrary excessively rigid blades will knock against the teeth causing the slackening of the plate on the lattice. In the blade, V-shaped slots are cut out with a pitch corresponding to the pitch of the teeth on the spiked lattice or on the opening roller. This is made to ensure a better removal of fibre from the teeth of the spiked lattice. Cleaning rollersare repaired in the same way as doffer rollers.

text: The evening rolleris made of a steel shaft carrying three disks towhich sixsteel blades with thick riveted-over needles are attached. In the course of the work the needles become loose and bent. At the time of repair, the faulty needles are cut-off and new needles 24 (Fig. 486) are fixed in place. The spiked rolleris m a d e of a steel pipe with flanges. The cylindrical part of the pipe has four rows of beveled spikes (the angle of inclination is 10°). W h e n the spikes are deteriorated they are cut away, the point of cut is dressed and new spikes 3 (Fig. 48c) are arc-welded. The point of welding is filed or sand-papered. The automatic bale feeder has seven spiked rollers. Each spiked roller has a shaft which carries disks and plates with spikes 4 (Fig. 48d) attached to these disks. Deteriorated spikes are replaced by new ones.

text: When repairing rollers of all kinds care should be taken that all spikes or needles are of the same height and the rollers have the same exterior diameter. The blade beater is a shaft with cross-pieces carrying steel trapezoidal plates. These plates have a reserve edge so that at blunting (wear) of the working edge the plate may be turned round and the reserve edge is used as a working one. After both edges have been used, the plate is removed and machined on a planer (the angle of edge inclination is 75°). The edge should be well defined but not sharp and its plane must pass through the centre line of the beater shaft. The restored blade 3 (Fig. 49) is attached on the spider 4 by means of a bevel screw 1 and locked with a dowel 2. The point of fixing to the spokes is carefully finished.

If in this case, the blade must be made heavier, then building-up may be carried-out from the interior side of the blade. The width of the weld must be narrower than that of the blade back plane and must have an oval surface. If at balancing of a three-blade beater it appears that one blade is heavier than the other, it must be planed. Modern scutchers are provided with saw-toothed or needle threeblade beaters, as smooth blade beaters do not ensure efficacious cleaning and separation of staples. text: Considering that the fibre passes over the surface of the pedals, high requirements are set towards their quality. Small pits are soldered with tin and carefully smoothened. The surface profile of the pedals is worked strictly to the template. Wear of pedals should not exceed 1 mm, otherwise they should be replaced by new ones (the whole set should be replaced at once). The side surfaces of the pedals should have no ledges and cavities are soldered with tin. The total width of pedals should be 2 m m less than the machine width. It is necessary to keep under observation the uniform and tight adherence of the pedals to the cylinders (the clearance should not exceed 0.2- 0.4 mm). The maximum stroke of the pedals (their lowering) in respect to the feeding cylinder should not be under 12 mm.

text: The pedals rest on a prism which must be strictly rectilinear and should have no surface indentations and other defects. The bent prism is dressed and, if damaged, soldered with tin. Prior to its installation the prism is carefully checked by the template (Fig. 51), cleaned and wiped with graphite. The template consists of a metal plate 2 with a shackle 4 and foot 5. The templates are attached on the feeding cylinders 3 using the plumb bob 1. If the depression on the foot accurately rests on the prism 6it means that the latter is set properly. All the system of pedal pendants, links and levers is checked for proper mating and mobility of joints. If the joints are worn more than 0.3 mm, the parts should be replaced.

text: Assembly and adjustment of the blowing range. At the assembly of the blending feeders and head feeders, all spiked and transport lattices must be disposed symmetrically relative to the machine centre line and should not catch its side walls. The same concerns the roller, beaters, calender and lapping rollers and cages. Sagging of the lattice and falling-out of the fibre are not allowed. The blades must be reliably fixed to the belts. The evening roller is installed according to a level and the roller teeth must be in the middle of the space between the spikes of the lattice. The leather covering the cleaning and doffing rollers should not catch the lattice spikes. The blade roller must be set strictly horizontally (according to a level) and must be properly balanced. Deteriorated (bent) grid bars are not to be put in place and only polished grid bars may be installed.

text: The production of modern cards manufactured in the USSR is 10-40 kg/h. The card consists of the feeding arrangement, the main cylinder and doffer, the flats, the doffing comb, the transmissions and the coiler. Prior to putting the cards in repairs, the wastes are eliminated, the card is dedusted and cleaned. At the time of intermediate repairs of cards the following work is performed in the following units: thefeedingarrangements— the back part of the card is disassembled, the taker-in cylinder is removed, the saw-toothed band is repaired and deburred. The taker-in bearings are dismantled and they are checked for good condition. The flanges are deburred and fastenings are checked, the grid bars are removed and restored, and the burrs on the receiving table are ground. The bearings and journals of the feeding cylinder are checked and deburred, the mote knives are exa­

text: Different operations (dimension control, building-up, fixing of repair bushings, replacement and repairs of bearings and others) may be carried out on the cylinder after raising it by means of jack. If the antifriction bearing is out of order the shaft of the taker-in, main cylinder or doffer comes also out of order. In this case, the bearing is replaced by a new one for which the shaft is turned, a split bearing is fitted on the shaft and over it an antifriction bearing preliminarily heated to a temperature of 70-90°C (in mineral oil). The device for turning the said shaft on the card (Fig. 53a) has a base 1 which is fixed instead of the removed bearing shell. text: During card repair, the sliding bearings are frequently replaced by antifriction bearings. For this, the bearing shell is extended and a cover is made which is attached with several screws. In the course of operation the bushings of the licker-in side plates are gradually worn-out due to which the reaches between the taker-in and feeding table, the main cylinder grid bars and knives are impaired. At the time of repair, the side plate with a worn-out bushing is replaced by a new or restored one. The worn-out bush is cut off and in the side plate a recess is bored into which a new bushing is pressure-fitted and tightened with four dowels. Covering with card fillet. In cards the main cylinders and doffers are covered with a whole-metal saw-toothed or needle fillet, while the licker-ins are covered with a saw-toothed fillet. The cleaners and workers are also covered with a whole-metal fillet.

text: To determine the dynamic parameters of the card cylinders in practice, instruments are used with an electromagnetic parametrical system in which the cylinder acts as a core (Fig. 55). With a change in the air gap 6 between the core and the bobbin (i.e. with some impairment in the surface of the cylinder covered with a whole-metal sawtoothed fillet) the inductivity of the bobbin is modified which is immediately recorded by an oscillograph. In this way, it is possible to determine the reaches between the main cylinder and the flats. A new method has been elaborated for the operative control of reaches between the fillets of the card working organs both at halts and in operation. Plates 5-12 m m in diameter and 3 to 5 m m in thickness of a material with high plasticity (ceresin or paraffin) are used as recording elements. text: After covering the cylinder with fillet the evenness and run-out of its toothed surface is checked. The evenness of the covering along the generatrices is checked by means of a rule and feeler, while the run-out is checked by a special instrument operating on the contactless principle. If the fillet teeth are of different height, the protruding teeth are machined with a needle file, while bent teeth are straightened by a grinder. For levelling the surface the filleted cylinders are ground.

text: Further balancing is carried out, i.e. the licker-in and the doffer are subjected to static balancing, while the main cylinder is dynamically balanced. The static balance of the doffer is checked by turning it in its proper bearings from which the lubricant has been preliminarily removed. In doing so, the heavy weight points causing the disbalance are detected. The doffer is balanced by means of weights fixed to attachments: the doffer comes out of balance when a weight of not more than 50 g is tangentially attached to it. The licker-in is subjected to static balancing on knife edges by attaching the balancing weight to its bottoms; a balanced licker-in is disbalanced when a weight up to 30 g is attached to it.

text: Drawing frame combs. In wool and flax spinning mills drawing frames are provided with combs consisting of a plate with pressure fitted round needles. At the ends of the comb plate there are provided chamfers by means of which the combs penetrate between the worm coils. In the course of operation, the comb chamfers are worn-out, the needles are broken, fall out of the plate which also comes out of order. The combs with worn-out chamfers are restored by gas or electric-arc welding, and in the event of small wear by the electric spark method. The metal overlay is ground. The deteriorated needles are eliminated and new ones are pressure fitted in their place.

text: For the adjustment of the roving frame after the assembly it must be set in idle running. During idle running it is essential to check the smooth operation of the roving frame, the heating-up of separate parts and units and to ascertain that there are no foreign noises during the running. Further, the spindle and bobbin rails are checked for horizontality. The stroke of the traverse should be equal to 75% of the working length of the shafts in the back line, and the distance between the extreme positions of the roving to the shaft ends should be equal. The centre lines of the bevel drums should be strictly parallel and in the same plane. F L U T E D R O L L E R S . In the course of roving frame operation the fluted rollers are bent, their journals are worn-out, the flutes become damaged and breakages occur at the places of threaded joints.

text: At machine repair, the rollers are removed from their bearings and placed on supports arranged along the machine. The line of rollers consists of staffs connected by threads. Several jacks are used simul­ taneously for removing the rollers. The rollers taken off from the roving frames are separated in staffs and each staff is checked with an indicator for determining which of them is bent and needs dressing. The roller staffs are dressed by means of a cramp on a lathe, a press or in a special machine. After dressing the roller run-out at the exterior surface of the fluted sections should not exceed 0.1-0.12 m m . If the supporting journals of the fluted roller are worn-out, they are restored by chromium plating, metal coating or building-up.

text: Rollers with a deteriorated fluted surface are repaired as follows. Different shallow scratches, indentations and burrs are eliminated with a needle file or trihedral scraper and then the rollers are polished with a paste of thin abrasive powder mixed with pure mineral oil. Worn-out flutes of unhardened rollers are restored by plastic deformation, by rolling over the cavities with a steel hardened roller 8— 0360 114 Chapter Five under a high pressure. Worn-out flutes of hardened rollers are fl!h deepened by a thin abrasive wheel or a shaped tool of hard alloys in a slitter using a grinding head instead of the top carriage. To restore the service ability of the fluted roller it is sufficient to remove from the cavity a layer of 0.08-0.1 mm. i*' -t

text: SPINDLES. In the course of operation spindles may be bent, heels, necks and seating cones of the flyers may become worn outr the slots for the flyer and eyelets may break. The bent spindle is straightened under press on a straightener or by means of different devices. (a) (b) Fig. 70. Device for repairing roving frame spindles The deteriorated spindle heel m a y be repaired by different methods. The spindle end is annealed and dressed on a lathe to obtain the required cone after which the spindle is hardened again and machined. Another more efficacious method consists in grinding without preliminary annealing and with subsequent hardening, but this method requires the use of a special device. When repairing spindles with worn-out heels, care should be taken that the height of spindles in one set used in a roving frame does not differ more than by 1.5 m m .

text: The worn-out neck and seating cone for the flyer are chrome plated. The worn-out slot is repaired by soldering a layer of brass or by electrolytic steel plating. The spindles with broken eyelets are repaired as follows: if one eyelet is broken off (Fig. 70a), then an insert 1 is attached with two rivets 2 to its place. The points of joining should be soldered with brass or copper. If both eyelets are broken (Fig. 706), the spindle head is cut-off and a new head 1 is threaded to its place and the butt faces 2 are soldered with brass or copper. After soldering the head is carefully finished. The shift of the slot centre line in respect to the spindle centre line should not exceed 0.15 mm. The run-out in diameter of the fitting cone is 0.15 m m and the run-out in diameter of the fitting cone for the flyer, heel and cylindrical part should not exceed 0.07 m m .

text: Flyers are repaired in a shop where they are sent to after removal from the spindles. Prior to the repairs the flyers are cleaned from dirt and fluff manually and in special devices. After cleaning, the flyers are washed in a bath with a soda solution. Lately for cleaning flyers ultrasonic units have found application. Reburring of flyers is effected by means of a needle file or emery cloth. A special milling cutter with small teeth disposed on the interior cone is used for eliminating burrs from the flyer head. The milling cutter is fixed in the spindle of a drilling machine, and the flyer— in a special device on the table so that the flyer head is disposed opposite the milling cutter. On the displacement of the rotating milling cutter along the head of the flyer, the teeth remove a very thin layer as if scraping the head.

text: DIFFERENTIAL MOTION. The main function of the roving frame differential motion is the addition of component speeds, i.e. of the constant speed of the main shaft and the variable speed of bevel drums as well as the transmission of the speed to bobbins. The differential motion consists of main members (central gears and carrier) and satellites— gears with shafts moving in space. Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 119 In the course of the differential motion operation the following disarrangements may be observed: cracks and crushing of holes in the body and cover, wear of gear shafts, teeth and other rubbing surfaces of gears, wearing of bushes.

text: The gears with a shank and the gear shafts are carburized, hardened and ground to the seventh class of finish. Sometimes grinding and chromium plating are used. W h e n repairing gears with a spindle (due to the wear of the spindle) the deteriorated spindle is cut off, the gear is drilled, reamed and a thread is cut. Next, a new spindle with thread is manufactured, both parts are connected by threading and pinned. When the toothing of internal gears is worn out they are repaired by built-up with further machining on a gear shaper. If such machines are not available, machining is carried out on a pla­ ner with special devices. In the recent time when repairing the roving frame, the differential gears are mounted on antifriction bearings which considerably improves the reliability of the differentials and reduces parts consumption.

text: The worn pawls are replaced by new ones or repaired by buildingup. The slack fixture of the rocker blocks is tightened and the worn blocks are replaced by new ones. In order to ensure a more reliable fixing of the blocks 2 (Fig. 75) they are dovetailed on the swinging lever 1 and tightened with screws 3.As the reversing motion is assembled, the pawls and rockers are mutually adjusted so that each pawl contacts the rocker with its full working surface. In locked position the clearance between the pawl and the rocker should not exceed 0.2-0.25 mm; at change-over one of the pawls must perfectly be en- 420 Chapter Five gaged, while the other must simultaneously be disengaged, and vice versa. It is convenient to carry out the repairs and adjustment of the reversing motion on a special stand in a workshop.

text: ASSEMBLY AND ADJUSTMENT OF ROVING FRAMES. Asthe roving frames are assembled and adjusted the roller beam should be strictly in horizontal plane. The allowable deviations in cross and longitudinal directions should not exceed 0.1 mm per running metre of the beam. The drawing system should operate smoothly and without jerks. The feeding roll must be smooth and free of indentations and burrs. The slider of the roller stand must be easily displaced with an allowable clearance not in excess of 0.3 mm. The flyers are washed, examined, balanced and carefully ground. The bobbin rail is checked for horizontality with a plumb bob and the spindle rail with a template. The rail lift is checked according to the bobbin working height. The bobbin rail must move smoothly. The shafts of the bottom and top conical drums must be strictly parallel and in one plane. The drums should be easily rotated by hand.

text: The mechanism of the shifter must operate smoothly without jamming and the shifter must move over the full length of the conical drums. When the shifter is in the position corresponding to the beginning of winding, the weight on the reversing motion block must be in upper position. When the shifter is in opposite position, the weight must not touch the floor. It is necessary to check the reversing motion for easy running. All the spindle heads must be disposed on one horizontal line. The rollers must rotate easily, their surfaces must be properly ground and the loads on the rollers must be maintained strictly the same along the lines. text: HALF LAPS AND TOP COMB. In operation the needles of comb segments and comb strips are deteriorated or broken and the top combs are also broken. Faulty comb segments and top combs are repaired in a specialized shop. The comb segments are disassembled, the faulty strips are unsoldered, checked and straightened, the needles are set, soldered to the strips, washed, dried and scraped, the segments are assembled, checked with a gauge, and ground. The strips removed from the segment are graded, faulty needles are unsoldered and eliminated; the strips are checked for rectilinearity and distorted strips are straightened (dressed) in a straightening die. Setting of the needles is effected manually by means of a special device.

text: After setting, the needles are levelled in height by means of a h a m mer and a strip, fixing with screws the position of the latter. Next, the needles are soldered to the strip. The soldered combs are washed, dried, and scraped after which the assembly of half laps is started. At the assembly, the correct position of the strip is checked by passing a 1-mm thick lamellar gauge between the sharp ends of the needles and the setting strip. After the strips have been checked throughout all their length, they are definitely fixed in the segment slot. To accelerate the adjustment of strips, the assembled half lap is ground in a lathe using an eccentric mandrel (with central holes shifted by 1.8 mm). Owing to the center shift the required eccentricity in the position of needle points is obtained. After the assembly, the half lap is polished with circular brushes and oil.

The spinning frame is prepared for repairs by breaking-off the roving, eliminating half-ready products from the frame, doffing the yarn and dusting the frame. During medium repairs of ring spinning frames the following jobs are carried out on the following units: creelfor rovingbobbins— the creel is checked according to the skewer, faulty cup-shaped porcelain footsteps are replaced, the creel is reinforced, the rods are examined and the boards are repaired;

text: At capital repairs the machine frame is additionally checked using a cord, a ruler, a plumb bob, and a level; the drawing unit is completely disassembled as well as the machine drive, spindles, drum, tension rollers and yarn guides. All faulty parts are replaced or restored, the drum is balanced, the spindles and antifriction bearings are disassembled, washed and lubricated. At machine adjustment a special attention is paid to the tension arrangement, and the drive of the drum and spindles. The quality of repairs is assessed by the quality of produced yarn, its proper win­ ding of the tube and the breakage rate.

text: For roller stands of drawing units in flax spinning frames, bronze bushings are used. The wear of these bushings results in non-coaxiality of their position as well as in excessive bending and run-out of weighted fluted rollers. In repair, it is essential to use plastic inserts (bushings) of antifriction material, which are ten times cheaper than bronze bushings. Moreover, as experience shows, it is efficient to use cylindrical bushings with a lug (Fig. 79) protecting the bushing from shifting. All the set of roller stands on the frame (irrespective of the design of the drawing unit and the type of spinning frames) must have bushings of the same size corresponding to the diameter of the fluted roller necks.

text: Fluted rollers. In combination with top rollers, the fluted rollers serve for the attenuation of sliver or roving. According to their position in the drawing unit, the roller staffs are subdivided into head, intermediate and off-end staffs, and correspondingly the rollers are provided with different flutes (trapezoidal, rhombic, etc.). In the course of operation the journals, necks and fluted surfaces of the rollers are subjected to twisting, bending and rubbing, which can provoke the following disarrangements: residual bend, wear of Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 127- necks, crushing and breakage of tails and seats of the staffs and wear of fluted surfaces.

text: Residual bending is due to the overloading of the roller or to its improper assembly (when the line of rollers does not rest on all the bearings). The rollers are checked for run-out using a special indicator directly on the spinning frame. The necks are worn because of insufficient lubrication and low rigidity of the roller line. The tails are broken due to the lack of proper threading in the staff seats. The fluted surfaces of the rollers are worn down by rubbing with the top rollers, when the web is cut with a knife or hook and also when the flutes are impaired by the yarn due to the insufficient displacement of the yarn guiding rule. text: Prior to starting the repair of fluted rollers, it is necessary to disconnect the staffs. This is achieved by means of a special wrench with, three cover plates articulated together for the tight gripping of the surface of the roller staff. The roller staffs are disconnected directly on the frame by means of two wrenches. Figure 80a illustrates another device for disconnecting the roller staffs. Grippers A consisting of two halves 1 and 3 (Fig. 806) are fixed from both sides of the point in which the staffs are to be disconnected. Each gripper has a lug with a saw-cut slit for the wrench. Both halves of the gripper are joined on the smooth necks of the rollers by a collapsible hinged bolt 4. Next, the rollers are placed on special supports 2 (Fig. 80a) and using wrenches applied on the grippers 5 (Fig. 806) the staffs are disconnected.

text: Straightening of bent rollers may be effected either manually (using a jimmy, sledge or straightening clamp) or by means of different devices which ensure a better quality and higher efficiency of repairs. Figure 81 illustrates a machine for straightening bent fluted rollers. text: The restoration of worn roller necks m a y be effected by different methods. If the rollers have been subjected to surface hardening by high-frequency currents, or carburizing and hardening, the wear in •diameter does not exceed 0.1 m m . In this case, the initial dimensions of the necks are restored by building-up in an electroplating bath with a coat of chromium up to 0.08 m m thick from each side. The necks of unhardened rollers are liable to have a greater wear (>0.01 m m ) and therefore they are restored by building-up with electrodes or by metal spraying. The rollers may also be restored by applying a layer of polyamide material (capron) under pressure. Sometimes regrinding of worn roller necks is done to obtain a new size (repair dimensions), Repair and Adjustment of Spinning Equipment 129 and adequate bearing linings are chosen to suit the new dimensions. text: The eccentricity of the thread must not exceed 0.15 mm and there must be no play at the points of connection. Local clearances should not exceed 0.25 of the circumference length and should not allow the passage of a feeler over 0.05 m m thick. In checking the roller staffs for rectilinearity, run-out, and twisting the allowable values should not be exceeded. Rollers with damaged fluted surface are to be restored by roll forming, planing, milling, grinding and chromium plating. When restoring the rollers by roll forming or knurling, their surface is subjected to the pressure of one or several steel hardened rollers owing to which the metal is redistributed according to the profile of knurling rolls. This method may be used only for unhardened fluted rollers (middle and back rollers of drawing units in cotton spinning frames).

text: The rollers of drawing units in flax spinning frames are machined on a planing machine equipped with an automatic divider, or on a longitudinal milling machine by means of a shaped milling cutter. To restore hardened rollers they must priorly be annealed and on restoring of the flutes they must be subjected to heat treatment. H o w ever, this kind of processing is costly and time consuming. For this reason, in such cases a flute planer is used with a divider and a grinding head attached in the planer stock. At the restoration of fluted rollers made of stainless steel (for flax wet spinning frames) a double chromium plating is applied which allows a 30 to 40 percent increase in the rollers life and ensures an economy in expensive stainless steel.

In grinding, the surface of the elastic cot must not heat above 80°G, as otherwise the structure and property of the rubber are badly impaired. For this reason, grinding is effected in two stages: first, coarse grinding leaving an allowance of 0.2-0.4 m m for further machining and next fine grinding. After grinding it is recommended to powder the roller with mica or other similar material. The roughness of the ground top rollers should not exceed 0.4-0.6 pm. Fig. 87. text: In the course of elastic cot surface grinding there might be deviations from the preset cylindrical shape and dimensions, i.e. eccentricity, faceting, and conicity. Eccentricity (Fig. 87a) is caused by the misalignment of the mandrel and worn centre holes. The allowable eccentricity for soft cots is 0.3 m m and for hard ones— 0.02 mm. Facetingm a y be caused by an excessive pressure applied at grinding (Fig. 87b). The allowable deviations in radii R-r for soft cots is 0.03 m m and for hard ones— 0.02 mm. Conicityresults from the improper adjustment of grinders. It is especially evident on long cots (Fig. 87c). For fixed rollers the conicity in diameters D-d must not exceed 0.06 m m and for loosely rotating ones — 0.04 mm. To increase the service life the rubber and P Y C top rollers should be turned. text: The surface processing of elastic cots reduces the surface irregularities and consequently improves the operational features of the cots. On heat treatment of elastic rubber cots, their surface layer becomes smooth and glossy. The optimum conditions for thermal treatment of rubber cots are: a temperature of 300°C and time of treatment— 10 s. A method has been developed for the thermomechanical treatment of elastic cots by a progressive increase in the temperature from 200 to 400°G. In this case, the coated rollers are rolled between plates for 25-35 s on the machine at different heating temperatures. The use of cots subjected to such heat treatment increases their life by 30%.

text: Bent spindle blades are repaired by straightening. To begin with, the point and amount of deflection are determined. For this, the spindle blade is placed on knife edges or fixed between the centres of the lathe, after which the spindle blade is turned around its axis and the point and amount of deflection are determined by means of an indicator. For straightening bent spindles the so-called static method is used, while for straightening spindles with an inconsiderable residual deflection the dynamic method finds application. text: For repairing worn spindles the following methods are used: regrinding, chromium plating, metal plating, building-up, as well as mechanical methods of repairing and restoring with polymer materials. Most often the wear of spindle heel results in deformation of its shape. The spindle with a worn heel is regroundby means of a special device or on a machine using intensive cooling. In chromium plating the surface of worn-out spindles is prepared for the job of grinding on a circular grinder. Next, the spindles are mounted on a suspension, degreased, chromium plated, washed, neutralized and taken off from the suspension. Provided the spindle surface has been thoroughly prepared for chromium plating no further machining is required after plating.

text: Big and heavy spindles are restored by the building-up method. Prior to building-up the spindles are annealed in a furnace for several hours at a temperature of 740-760°C and left in the same furnace for cooling. After cooling, a small layer of metal is removed with a cutter so as to obtain the required thickness of the built-up layer (1-2 mm). Building-up is carried out by the gas-flame method using a neutral flame by means of a burner of reduced power (by 1-2 Nos.). The built-up spindle is forged, roasted and machined on a lathe leaving an overlap for grinding of 1-1.5 m m taking into account the possibility of strong warping at the subsequent heat treatment (hardening and tempering). In some cases, to repair worn-out spindle heels different mechanical methods are applied, including the replacement of heels (skeleton spindles). text: Tbe vibration (run-out) is determined directly on the spinning frame by means of an indicator (Fig. 90). The watch type indicator 1 is fixed on the rocker 2 with a hinged support 3 arranged on the bracket 4,which is provided with an adjusting screw 7, nuts, and a stop screw 6.The instrument is fixed as a C-clamp on the spindle rail 5 of the spinning frame. The indicator is set by means of the adjusting screws strictly on the vertical line passing through the centre of the drum which is manually rotated. If the radial run-out of the drum does not exceed 0.7 mm, it may be considered fit for operation. All other defects are detected by inspection and ifit proves necessary the drum is repaired in a special shop. Prior to starting the repair, the tape is removed from the tension roller, as well as 4 or 5 spindles disposed opposite the intermediate bearings of the drum.

The watch type indicator 1 is fixed on the rocker 2 with a hinged support 3 arranged on the bracket 4,which is provided with an adjusting screw 7, nuts, and a stop screw 6.The instrument is fixed as a C-clamp on the spindle rail 5 of the spinning frame. Prior to starting the repair, the tape is removed from the tension roller, as well as 4 or 5 spindles disposed opposite the intermediate bearings of the drum.

text: If the repair of a damaged drum is unfeasible, the drum members are replaced by new ones. In this case, the old m e m ber is eliminated, while the new one is soldered and welded. When spare members are not available, they are produced in the shops of the textile enterprise. A blank is cut-out from a sheet of tin plate 1 (Fig. 94a) in accordance with the dimensions of the member, and passed between the rollers 2 and 3 to impart it a cylindrical shape after which the ends are flanged. Further, the seams are soldered and welded with overlapping (in a spot- and seam welding machine) and carefully dressed. Ready members must engage each other without play. The reinforcement diaphragms are made of the same material as the drum shell. The diaphragm blank is cut out of a sheet and extruded by means of a pressing mould (Fig. 94&) attached in the spindle of the lathe.

text: Static balancing of drums is carried out on knife-edges. The drum is set with its spindles on the knife-edges and rotated manually. If the drum is not properly balanced, its heavier part always comes to occupy the bottom position. In this case, a recess is made on the opposite side of the drum and filled by soldering with lead until the d r u m is statically balanced. Next, the dynamic balancing of the d r u m is carried out in a special machine (Fig. 95). The drum 4 is placed with its spindles on two split bearings 3 having a prismatic base. One half of the coupling 2 is fixed to the end of the spindle and the second by means of a sliding key— on the driving shaft 1. Next, the motor isengaged to impart rotation to the drum through the pulley 8. Then the coupling is disengaged by the crank 7, i.e. the motion is not any more transmitted to the drum which continues to rotate by inertia.

text: At the same time, one of the bearings is released from rigid fixing (the bolts 5 are loosened). If the drum is not properly balanced the released bearing deviates from initial position and causes the deformation of the spring 6.The heavy part of the drum which has provoked this deviation is marked with chalk. A recess is made on the opposite side of the drum to be filled with lead to achieve drum balancing. With this aim it is possible to use a rubber tyre which is fitted on the drum. After determining which of the drum sides is heavier, a weight is placed under the tyre at its opposite side. By displacing the weight and changing its mass the necessary solder mass and points ofsoldering are determined. Further, all the soldered points are carefully dressed. Balancing is done at high rotational speed of the drum (10% higher than the working rotational speed).

text: Special fitter’s shops are provided at the mills for repairing the spinning heads of spinning frames B^-200. Every fitter in the shop has a specially equipped bench with an electric instrument for checking the sensor and the centrifuge as a whole. Mounted on the bench are pivotable mechanisms for installing the centrifuges in any required position, and plug sockets are provided for connecting vacuum cleaners and soldering irons. text: Every shop has a work bench provided with vices, tables and a tester for accurate checking of the centrifuge electrical parts. The efficient cleaning of centrifuges is ensured by vacuum cleaners and the tables are equipped with a system for the removal of contaminated air and dust. The centrifuges are transported from the spinning frame to the shop in three-deck trucks accommodating up to 50 spinning heads. Multi-deck racks are available for storing 600 spinning heads. The periodicity of centrifuge repairs in the case of the spinning frame B^-200 is as follows: overhaul— every year (duration— five days); medium repair— every six months (duration 2.5 days); thorough cleaning— every three months (duration one day). At thorough cleaning the spinning heads are cleaned and checked directly on the spinning frame.

section: R e p a i r a n d A d j u s t m e n t o f T e x t i l e M a c h i n e s
text: Because the feeding unit cannot be disassembled, it must be completely replaced when its parts come out of order. The state of the combing drum 6 is determined by the condition of its closing. Its main disarrangements are brokenteethand deterioration of the whole-metal saw-toothed fillet. In this case the combing drum is replaced by a new one. 10 IHi1 Fig. 97, Diagram of spinning head in open-end spinning frame The twisting and building unit consists of the centrifuge 3 rotating on a shaft, the bearing 4 and separator 5. The main disarrangements are: contamination, oil penetration and carbon deposit. In this case, the centrifuge is replaced by a new one. Bearings wear and loose separator fastenings are also a frequent case.

text: At the assembly of the spinning head in an open-end spinning frame it is necessary to check with a special feeler the clearance of the electromagnetic clutch of the feeding unit, as the proper engagement and disengagement of the feeding cylinder depend on thisclearance. It is also important to check the proper installation of the yarn breakage sensor (in particular, using a special gauge it is ascertained that the carrier does not impede the passage of the yarn into the centrifuge at mass threading). It is observed that in open-end spinning frames Bfl-200-M69 the yarn sometimes winds on the drawing-off roller causing its scoring. This results in a higher breakage rate and lower yarn quality. For grinding the drawing-off roller the spinning frame should be stopped and the roller taken off.

text: Vulcanizer for belt glueing. It has proved efficacious to glue the belts of open-end spinning frame B71,-200-M69 which have come out of order. For this, a special vulcanizer is used consisting of the housing 1 (Fig. 99), the shell 7, terminal 2, insulator 3, cover plate 4, heating element 5 (for 24 V), jimmy bar 8,clip 9 and thrust bearing 10. Prior to glueing the belt is machined to conical shape over a length of 40 mm. Next, it is coated with glue, inserted in the vulcanizer, pressed with bolts 6 and after switching-on the current kept at least two hours at a temperature of 110-120cC. The glue employed for belt glueing consists of hydraulic alcohol, resercine and formic acid ethyl ether.

text: The device operates as follows: the centrifuge 12 is placed into the interior part 9 of the chamber 5 so as to obtain that the shell 10 bears with its butt face against the gasket 8 and the pulley 77 bears against the gasket 6. Using the lever 13, the centrifuge 12 is pressed by means of the spring 15 and fixed in place by the locator 14. The butt faces of the shell and pulley must be tightly pressed to the gaskets to avoid the leakage of lubricant through the clearances bypassing the cavity of the shell 10. Using the crank 20, the grease is pumped by the injector 19 through the holes 4 and pipe union 7 into the cavity of the chamber 5, i.e. into the zone of the pulley 77 between the gaskets 8 and 6. As a result the grease passes under pressure through the clearances into the cavity of the shell 10, and displacing the old grease lubricates the bearings.

text: The condensing roll serves for compacting the winding on the warper’s beam. It consists of the left half 1 (Fig. 101) and right half 4 of the cylinder connected together by the steel ring 3 (new models of warpers are equipped with whole-metal condensing rolls of stain­ less steel). Inside the cylinder at its ends there are bolted cast-iron rims 7which serve for braking the condensing roll. The ball bearings 6 are attached on the disks 5 secured to the rims; these bearings are fixed in conical bushings on the shaft 2 around which the condenser roller is rotating. During warping the condenser roller is constantly displaced deep into the machine (progressively with the increase of winding diameter of the warper’s beam). Warper's beam change mechanism. Intended for rapid and easy replacement of the full warper’s beams.

text: The warper’s beam consists of the stemi (Fig. 102) made of steel pipe 240 m m in diameter. At the stem ends there are screwed or threaded 800 m m dia. flanges 2 cast of light alloys. Couplings 3 attached by pins and screws with the stem are inserted in grooves provided inside the pipe at its ends. Locks 4 for joining the warper’s beam with tailstock sleeves are screwed to the couplings. The steel axle 5carrying the ring 6 for reliably fixing the locks on the axle is inserted into the locks and the ring itself is pinned on the axle. The flanges are cast as a whole with the pulleys 7 serving for braking the warper’s beams on the sizing machine. The flanges are provided with reinforcement ribs. The run-out of a 240-mm diameter stem must not exceed 0.5 m m and the end play of flanges 800 m m in diameter must not exceed 1 mm.

text: The drum of the first type warping machine is a whole-metal cylindrical part with a cone the angle of which changes from 6 to 26°. The cylinder is made of aluminium sheet, and the variable cone consists of 24 telescopic wedges. The cone angle is modified by means of a leverage system and a movable coupling. The drum of the second type warping machine is a whole-metal cylinder with a constant cone. The cylinder and cone are made of aluminium sheets and from both sides the drum is provided with belt brakes ensuring the rapid stoppage of the machine and normal braking of the drum in warp beaming. The brake is equipped with an automatic regulator to maintain a constant warp tension in beaming. The braking force is adjusted by the brake regulator. The warping table consists of a carriage with a reed, a measuring ruler, a friction clutch and a bracket for mounting the static elimin­

text: The drum startingmechanism effects the engagement and stoppage of the machine. The engagement and disengagement are effected from one treadle running along the machine. The mechanism has treadle levers loosely fitted on the shaft. Through pawls they are connected with the unbraking levers and are fixed in working position by a locator connected with the electromagnet and disengagement pawl. The counter mechanism ensures machine stoppage after a preset number of revolutions and when a complete section isfinished. A tachometer is provided to determine the warping speed. The warp length counter and tachometer are actuated from the drum through a chain drive, a friction speed variator and a reducer; and the counter of revolutions— from the drum through a chain drive, a reducer and a worm couple. 0500rdfid 0 P0 n d00 d00 fl •H X

text: The coil is attached in the slot of the shell by means of a grouting mass on the basis of epoxy resin. A plastic insulation ring with a pressure-fitted contact ring inside it is mounted on the clutch shell. The reliable fixing of the insulation ring on the shell is ensured by knurling the seating surface, the use of epoxy resin glue and cylindrical pins. The contact ring ismade of steel hardened to Rockwell C 60-62 and reliably joined with the insulation ring made of fabricbased laminate or glass reinforced plastic. One outlet wire of the coil is soldered to the butt face of the contact ring and the other to the clutch bobbin. Friction disks are made of steel with a hardness of Rockwell G F i g . 1 1 1 . text: 40-45. Provided between the inferior disks are wave-shaped springs releasing the friction disks on clutch disengagement. The clutch armature consists of three parts. The interior bronze bushing insulates the armature from the shaft owing to which the dispersion of the magnetic flow through the shaft is reduced and the armature can freely move on clutch engagement and disengagement. The bronze bushing is pressure-fitted into the interior armature ring with which the exterior armature ring is joined with a clearance fit. This design, ensures tight adherence of the armature to the friction disks and compensates for the possible irregularity in the thickness of the pack of friction disks at the level of the inside and outside diameters.

text: The clutch is lubricated with industrial oil. Prior to filling the oil, the clutches as well as the tank must be carefully cleaned from fine chips, cast iron dust, etc. From 8 to 9 litres of oil are to be filled into the reducer, and the magnetic clutch disks must be immersed to 15-25 m m in the oil. The disk cooling and oiling would be much worse for the low oil level. The examination of oil condition and its level is done with the reducer cover removed and the machine at standstill. The lubricant oil ages quicker with the operation of units equipped with clutches than with gearings. For this reason, it is necessary to take care that the oil temperature in the tank does not exceed 50°C and should be maintained within the limits of 30-40°C. During the work it is necessary to establish the most adequate regularity of oil replacement.

First, the movable armature is fitted on the shaft and upon it in consecutive order: the external friction disk, the internal disk, then again an external disk carrying the first spring washer, and so on. The last internal disk is placed on the external disk and spring washer, and the clutch coil is put in place. It is not allowed to use deformed disks. The disks prior to installation are checked on a smooth Hat plate without dents and scratches and distorted disks must be straightened. text: The sizing machines are intended for applying the size on the warp yarns, squeezing out the excess of size, drying the warp yarns and winding them on the weaver’s beam with preset density. These machines are complex ranges equipped with devices for the automatic adjustment and control of processing parameters. The main parts of any sizing machine are: the creel for warper’s beams (or weaver’s beams); the framework and drive; the sizing unit, the drier, the separating rods and reed for separating the glued warp yarns; the winding mechanism, the measuring and marking mechanism, complementary arrangements (emulsifying unit or waxing unit); the automatic devices for controlling the sizing process and maintaining preset parameters.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: 192 Chapter Six means of squeezing rolls. The sizing unit consists of the framework, the tank for the size, the tank lifting mechanism, the immersion and measuring rollers, the top squeezing rubber-coated roll and the bottom squeezing metal roll (the driving one). A special tank with a size pipeline is provided for size circulation. Theframework is a structure made of two cast-iron stands mounted on a common welded frame of rolled steel, these stands being braced together. The framework carries all the assemblies and mechanisms of the sizing unit. Arranged inside the stand guards are the mechanism for lifting and lowering the immersion roller and the control panels of the tank lifting mechanism and of the squeezing roll pressure mechanism. During repair of the framework its rigidity is restored by welding the defectuous points.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The sizetank is made of stainless steel sheet. A special mechanism consisting of a double-stroke pneumatic cylinder and a leverage system ensures its lift and lowering. The tank is filled with size through two branch pipes of the size duct and also from the system supplying the size in the roller nip. The tank design ensures a const­ ant circulation of the size, i.e. the size coming into the tank from the reservoir reaches the level of the tank edge and overflows into the discharge opening, after which it is returned into the reservoir via the discharge mains. For discharging the size remaining below the level of the tank edge, an outlet is provided in the tank which is connected by pipelines with the circulation tank and the sewage.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The size remaining in the tank may be discharged back into the reservoir and the water after washing— into sewage. The aim of tank repairs is to eliminate possible leakages. After repair (welding) the joint tightness is checked by flooding the tank with water and the circulation pump and size duct are cleaned. The immersion roller (130 m m in diameter) is made of stainless steel and mounted in sliding friction bearings which are connected with the racks of the immersion roller lifting and lowering mechanism. The racks are actuated from the drive consisting of an a.c. motor and a worm reducer. The top and bottom positions of the immersion roller are fixed by end switches through the intermediate of two rests mounted on the right-hand rack. If necessary the bearings are replaced and the rack and rests are repaired.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The top squeezing rollmade of a steel pipe with an elastic rubber coating is mounted in antifriction bearings on the pressure mechanism levers. The top squeezing roll ispressed to the bottom one through a leverage system from two pneumatic chambers. A special locator is provided for fixing the roll in upper position when the machine is stopped for a long time. During the operation of the sizing machines cavities are formed on cast iron squeezing rolls which renders difficult the squeezing of warp yarns. To avoid this defect the roll is usually turned on a lathe, Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 193

For this, using a chisel, a hole is made at the point of the cavity and an aluminium rod of adequate diameter is inserted in this hole and riveted over (Fig. 113). This done the riveted cavity is filed. Fig. 113. Method of repairing squeez­ ing rolls of sizing machine The sizecirculation tank is made of stainless steel and consists of an exterior bath with an interior bath inserted into it. A coil with blind steam is arranged in the space between the two baths which is filled with glycerin (the latter being a heat carrier ensuring the uniform heating of the size in the tank). The repair of the tank comes to the restoration of its tightness. After repairs, the tank and coil are checked for good sealing.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The cylinder drier is intended for drying the warp to be impregnated with size and squeezed. It consists of the framework, several drying cylinders (5, 7, 9, 11 and more), two transfer rollers, a steam and condensate pipeline and the drying cylinders drive. The transfer roller at the entry into the drier and the first four or three cylinders have an antiadhesion coating (Teflon, fluoroplastic) to avoid the adherence of the size on the surface. The drierframework is a structure made of cast iron stands connected together by braces. The framework carries all the units and mechanisms of the drier.

text: The drying cylinder (Fig. 114) consists of the shell 7 m a d e of steel sheets. Elliptical bottoms 6 are welded to the shell and have flanges to which the journals 3 are attached. Provided on the left-hand journal is the silphon seal 4 for supplying the steam and elimination of the condensate, while on the right-hand journal there are the vacuum valve 2 and the driving sprocket 1. All drying cylinders are rotated by means of chain drive. In the bottom of the cylinders a discharge cock is provided for the elimination of the condensate.

section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: During repairs, a check is made on the drying cylinder ladles, the vacuum valves and the discharge cocks; the manholes of the cylinders are closed. When carrying out any work inside the drying cylinder measures are taken to avoid unrestricted supply of steam or condensate into the cylinder, i.e. the steam line and condensate lines are disconnected from the cylinders and reliable locks are provided on starting valves. The bearings are washed (one of the bearings must have an axial clearance of 4-5 m m so as to allow the free elongation of the cylinder shaft on heating). The balancing of cylinders is checked at the site and the insulation of their butt faces is restored. The delivery part of the machine consists of the framework, the ribbed roller, the delivery roll, the measuring and pressure rollers, 13-0360 ( b ) 196 Chapter Six

text: The loom mechanisms may be classified according to their application into three groups: (1) the main working mechanisms for the execution of the principal technological operations in the process of fabric formation (shedding and weft insertion motions, slay, fabric drawing-off and winding mechanisms, warp tensioning and releasing arrangements); (2) complementary working mechanisms taking no direct part in the process of fabric formation and mounted on the loom mainly for increasing its efficiency (the weft feeding mechanism); (3) safety mechanisms effecting control over loom operation, precluding fabric faults in case of disarrangements, and 200 Chapter Six protecting loom parts from breakage (warp and weft controllers, warp protection motion, etc.). Classification of looms. Looms are classified by the method of weft insertion in the shed and the method of fabric formation on the loom.

text: According to the method of weft insertion in the shed, the l o o m s are grouped into shuttle and shuttleless looms (AT)*. In their turn the shuttleless looms are subdivided into looms with smallweft inserters (type CTE>)**, pneumatic looms (type P) and hydraulic looms (type H)***, rapierand pneumatic rapier looms (type ATIIP)****. In shuttle looms the weft yarn is laid in the shed by a shuttle carrying a bobbin with a reserve of weft yarn. Unlike the shuttle looms, shuttleless looms effect weft laying by weft inserters (small size inserters, by water or air jet and by rapiers) which carry no reserve of weft yarn. In this case the weft yarn is unwound from big stationary packages disposed outside the shed.

text: The overhaul is carried out once in two or three years by a team of workers. In overhauling, the loom is completely disassembled, the worn-out parts are replaced and the units are checked and cleaned. After the overhaul, the loom technical condition slightly differs from a new one. If after the overhaul some old parts are left for further use, these parts must be restored to good technical condition and a special statement should be made in the reception certificate. The volume of work to be performed during medium repairs and ^general overhaul of looms is determined in special instructions. The foreman of the mechanical repair department stops the equipment for medium and general overhaul repairs at the dates called for by the repair schedule. Before submitting the looms to repairs, they must be cleaned and the gaited warp removed. Repair and Adjustment of Parts, Units and Mechanisms

text: Frames, Braces and Breast Beam The frames, braces and breast beam when assembled together form the loom framework. Usually they are cast of iron or steel. To ensure the adequate rigidity and stability of the framework, the frames and braces are provided with reinforcement ribs along the whole contour, thus forming a trough or double-Tee section. In the course of loom operation cracks, cuts, worn-out holes for shafts, inserts, etc. may be observed and breakages may occur. •Cracked and broken frames are repaired by welding or by machining. The welding method depends on the place of cracks and chipping. If they are disposed at sharp curvatures in the frame profile, hot electric arc welding (with preliminary heating) is used; while in all other places it is advisable to use cold welding.

text: In hot welding the places to be repaired are cleaned from dirt and oil, the crack is made up asan Y-shaped seam and at its sides .graphite plates are fixed in place with fire clay to protect melted cast iron from spreading about. The frame prepared in this way is .subjected to local heating to 600-650°C using a gas burner. The heated points are closed with an asbestos sheet and the cracks are welded after which the frame is slowly cooled and the seams finished. In coldwelding the points to be welded and the adjacent surface .are cleaned from dirt and oil after which Y-shaped bevels at an Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 203 angle of 90° are cut, their depth being equal to 0.25-0.5 frame wall

text: In CTB shuttleless looms and the ATIIP automatic rapier looms the braking force of the main shaft is adjusted by means of the bolt 7 (Fig. 117): to increase the main shaft braking the bolt is to be tightened and to reduce it the bolt must be loosened. Turning of the shaft by inertia at the moment of loom stoppage should not exceed 25°. For checking, the weft yarn is removed from the feeler of the weft controller and the main shaft is turned by hand— in this case the disengagement of all CTB shuttleless looms must occur when the main shaft has turned over 255° (but not later than at 280°). To avoid rubbing of the exterior part of the braking flywheel 5 against the braking belt 6 at the moment of shaft rotation, it is necessary to adjust a clearance of 0.5 m m over the entire circumference of the braking flywheel between the braking belt and the flywheel.

text: In high-speed pneumatic looms the drive parts are worn quicker than all the rest. Most often it proves necessary to replace the slotted shaft 1 (Fig. 118), the disk 2, the key 6, the rod 4, the bearing 5 and the ring 3.These parts may be easily restored by building-up the worn places by oxyacetylene welding with subsequent manual finishing or on a lathe. An exception to this are the slotted shaft 1 and disk 2 as pn the shaft 1 usually the slots are worn out and it is easier to replace the shaft, rather than to restore the slots. The slots are also worn in the disk 2,but they may be restored. For this a cut-out is made in the hub of the disk, a bushing is prepared and press-fitted inside with welding of edges followed by broaching the slots on a special machine. This kind of restoration is timeconsuming operation and therefore it is.resorted to very rarely.

text: Fig. 121. Diagram of motion transmission to healds Shedding motion of the CTB shuttleless and ATOP automatic rapier looms. As the shedding motion is adjusted, the angle of shed opening, the shed height relative to the comb teeth and the moment of shed closure are adjusted. The angle of shed opening may be from 18 to 26° depending on the kind of processed raw materials. During loom erection this angle is adjusted to 21°, for which the shackles 4 (Fig. 121) on the heald levers 3 are displaced downwards over a distance of a = 35 mm. The shed angle decreases with the increase in the dimension a and vice versa. The shed height in relation to the slay comb teeth is adjusted by modifying the dimension b which is usually set equal to 10-15 mm.

text: In the course of operation, the surface of the tappet is worn and cracks may appear. The distortion of the tappet contour brings changes in the law of heald displacement which m a y result in defectuous fabric. The worn surface of tappets are repaired by building-up with an allowance of 2 to 3 m m for further machining. First, after building up, the tappet surface is machined by grinding wheel and then finished according to a template on a lathe. As a template, is employed an accurately machined new tappet having a rim which is 3 or 4 m m greater than that of the repaired tappet (for cutter overrunning). The tappet to be repaired is imparted the same profile as the template. In turning, an allowance of 0.15-0.2 m m is provided for subsequent grinding on the lathe. The tappet profile is checked
