text: The high-speed C K H dobby consists of the following main parts and mechanisms: the frame, the drive, the heald driving mechanism, the knives turning mechanism and the programming mechanism. The main mechanism is the heald driving mechanism with jacks 2 and 15 (Fig. 124), the balks 4, the stationary rests 5 and 12, the movable rods 3 and 13, and leverage system 6-10. In accordance with the pattern design the jacks 2 of the top row or jacks 15 of the bottom row are set on the line of action of knives 1 and 14. The moving knife catches the jack and displaces it together with the balk 4. The middle part 02of the balk on its displacement shifts the heald through the intermediate of the carrier 11, shackle 7, rocker 6, lever 10, the latch 8 and the horizontal drawbar 9.

Jack rods are repaired by different methods depending on their design. For instance, worn pins are drilled out or cut away on a milling machine. text: The worn-out hole in the jack rod is drilled, reamed and a cast iron repair bushing is press-fitted inside. The worn-out flats are ground on a surface grinder and during assembly washers are inserted between them, the thickness of which is equal to the double thickness of the flat. The balks are liable to develop the following faults in the course of operation: the holes and pins are worn-out and the eyelets broken. The worn-out holes are drilled, reamed, and bushings are press-fitted inside them. Worn-out pins are built-up and filed. In other cases the worn-out pins are cut off on a milling cutter. In the place of the cut-off pin through-holes are drilled in which steel washers are riveted or steel rods are welded. Damaged eyelets are cut off and in their place new ones are welded or soldered after which holes are drilled and finished in the eyelets.

text: The knivesare liable to wear on the following places: the working surface of the shafts on which the jacks are operating, places on which knives rest on the frame guiding slots, and the ends to which the drawbars and draw jacks are attached. The worn-out working surface of the knife is built up and ground on an emery wheel and finished in a special device on a surface grinder in cross direction. The points where the knife rests on the frame guiding slots are built-up with cast iron. The built-up surface is worked to suit the slots and to ensure the easy displacement of the knives inside them. The worn-out ends of the knife are built up, ground and holes are drilled for cotter pins. In the course of operation the ends of jacks get worn or broken. The jack worn ends are built up and then carefully machined for proper fitting. Broken ends are welded.

As a result, there may occur wedging and consequently the breakage of mating parts. As the lubrication of sliders is difficult, it is good practice to make the sliders of a textile based laminate with oil impregnation (by keeping in an oil bath for 4-5 days). For the repair, adjustment and running-in of the dobby a special stand has been designed. text: The system for supply and distribution of compressed air in pneumatic looms* As the air supply system is repaired, it is frequently necessary to replace the air pipelines. Fig. 133 shows how the pipe end is to be prepared for replacement. The end of the pipe 1 of adequate length is tapered by filing and the nut 2 and pressure ring 3 are fitted upon it. Then, using a centre punch or any other bevel tool, the ends of the pipe are expanded thus forming the head 5. This pipe end is inserted into the hole of the coupling 4 and the nut 2 is fitted upon it pressing with its lug on the ring 3 thus shifting it 220 Chapter Six and pressing to the lugs of the coupling 4 the side face of the pipe 1. Next the nut 2istightened and a checking for air leakage is made. In case of air leakage the operation is repeated so as to completely eliminate it.

text: Welt laying mechanism in ATIIP automatic rapier looms. The mechanism operates as follows. Two tubular rapiers penetrate into the open shed from both sides of the loom. When the rapiers meet in the middle of the shed, the weft yarn passes from the right rapier to the left one and is laid up to the left-hand edge of the fabric. The weft yarn is unwound from a stationary fixed bobbin with a constant speed by means of a measuring mechanism. With the aid of a compensator the yarn is supplied at variable speed first into the righthand rapier and then to left-hand one. The rapiers are actuated by a drive and the air jets in the right- and left-hand rapiers are created either by an individual compressor mounted on each loom or by a centralized air supply system. The weft laying mechanism consists of three parts: the rapier displacement mechanism, the weft

text: With the loom in the same position, the rapiers are checked for maximum rarefaction. For this, the hose connected with the compound pressure-and-vacuum gauge is fitted first on the nipple of the right-hand rapier and the nipple is turned until a zero reading is obtained on the gauge scale. For creating the vacuum, the nipple is tightened clockwise over a quarter of a turn at which the pressureand-vacuum gauge readings should not be under 25 kPa. Next, the hose from the pressure-and-vacuum gauge is introduced through the shed and fitted on the pointed end of the left-hand rapier. Turning the nipple a maximum vacuum is created in the rapier; the readings of the pressure and vacuum gauge should not be under 10 kPa. After the adjustment of the rapiers is completed, the loom must be released from the stop and the guards are to be closed.

text: When replacing the gland body in slay boxes or the gland in the frame, the latter is pressed out from the slay box. For this, in the side face of the gland body, holes are drilled with a thread M6 cut inside. The screws are then turned into the holes so as to have their side face butting against the ball bearing shell. On further rotation of screws, the gland body is pressed out. After the gland has been repaired and its body press-fitted in the slay box, the drilled holes are closed by screws and glue to avoid oil leakage. The slay mechanism ol shuttle looms. The slay mechanisms may be subdivided into fast reed and loose reed mechanisms; mainly a crank fast reed slay mechanism finds application.

text: The reed attached in the slay beam is subjected to considerable loads especially in high speed looms (up to 1000 N and more) and also to vibrations. Moreover, the reed dents are rapidly worn out by running against the warp yarns. The main disarrangements of the reed are: the failure of soldered seams, slackening of fixtures, shattering and breakage of dents. The longevity and reliability of reeds m a y be increased by using reinforced (wider) chromium-plated dents (of 4 m m rather than 2.8 m m wide), or by employing glues instead of soldering to fix the reed dents. The second method is the most efficacious from the point of view of reed reliability. Moreover, the Repair and Adjustment of Weaving Machinery 231

text: The adjustment of the warp protector motion must be carried out so as to satisfy certain requirements. The stop rod must easily rotate in bearings and its longitudinal shift must not exceed 1 mm. At the moment when the warp protector nibs exercise their action on the stop pad frogs, the distance from the fabric fell to the reed must be 65-67 mm. (Knocking of the warp protector nibs against the frogs.) The distance between the warp protector pad and the frame must be equal to 20 mm. At the moment when the warp protector nibs come in contact with the pads, the latter should move forward not more than 10 m m , as otherwise knocking against the frame can occur. W h e n the shuttle completely enters into the shuttle box, the warp protector nibs should be 2-3 m m above the stop pad frogs.

The warp delivery or let-off motion used in these looms is of the negative action, i.e. it lets off the warp from the weaver’s beam depending on the tension applied. This motion is designed to maintain the adequate tension of the warp and to ensure its automatic supply in accordance with the fabric winding by the cloth take-up motion. text: Planetary regulator or selected let-off motion. At the installation and adjustment of the planetary regulator, it is necessary to observe the following recommendations. The regulator shaft 1 (Fig. 144) and the roller 17 of the warp feeler must easily rotate in the bearings without misalignment and longitudinal shift. The weaver’s beam gear 27 and the underbeam gear 25 must mesh with their initial circumferences so as to have a clearance of 2 m m between the head of the teeth on one gear and the tooth root on the other gears. Both gears must be flush in width. The flange of the beam 26 must not contact the underbeam gear 25,the bottom link 23must easily rotate on the regulator shaft and the top link 5 on the spindle 6. No longitudinal displacement of links is allowed.

When the weaver’s beam is empty, and the feeler foot rests on the beam pipe, the link roller 4 must not fall out from the link slots and must be 4-5 m m above the bottom slots. text: The bottom link is adjusted in working position with the slay in extreme front position and the warp released. The link is adjusted so that it butts with its upper arm against the limiter arranged in the bottom part of the left-hand frame. At this, the eyelet 20 is rigidly connected with the drawbar 21 leaving a clearance of 2-3 m m between the interior surface of the eyelet slit and the exterior surface of the finger 19. Next, the slay is shifted in extreme back position at which the finger 19 must easily and freely move in the eyelet slit and the eyelet must shift in the direction of slay sword movement only under the action of the back rest 11. The drawbar 21 and eyelet 20 must not contact the roller 17. For increasing the warp tension the springs 8 and 7 are clamped by the nuts 16.

text: In the warp delivery motion the most liable parts subject to wear are the gear shafts, the braking wheel 7, the adjusting bolt 5, the brake block 2 and the shaft 3. The mechanism parts which have been removed during disassembly should be washed and cleaned from fluff and dirt (especially the gear toothing). All the other parts are replaced when they are worn out. The glueing of plugs on the brake block is facilitated by a simple arrangement. The brake blocks are fitted on a rod and a metal plate is pressed above by wing nuts leaving them in this position for 15-20 hours until the glue has completely dried.

text: Technical felt on the pressure roller 4 is rarely worn out over its whole surface and most frequently its right-hand side is worn out and replaced. To ensure a better fastening of the felt on the rollerr a complementary winding of one or two fabric layers may be made and impregnated with joiner’s glue. To avoid folds a whole piece of technical felt should not be wound on the pressure roller. The felt should be cut in strips 80 m m wide and 5400 m m long. section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The loom adjustment may most easily be discussed by correlating the action of its mechanisms with only one unit the operation of which is strictly determined and does not depend on the operation of all other mechanisms and devices. Such a working unit is the loom main shaft, one revolution of which corresponds to the loom working period, i.e. to the period when one fabric element is formed. The circumference corresponding to one revolution of the main shaft is divided by 360°, and the extreme front position of the reed is adopted as the beginning of motion, i.e. the moment of weft beating-up to the fabric felt. Expressing the beginning, duration and end of loom mechanism action by means of the main shaft angle of rotation, we obtain a cyclogram of loom operation.

CHAPTER 7 METHODS AND KINDS OF REPAIRS OF TEXTILE EQUIPMENT 1. Methods of Textile Machinery Repairs The repair methods employed determine the procedures carried out during the restoration of textile machinery. There are two main kinds of repair methods: the individual repair method and the unit repair method.

product: Tekstil makineleri onarım ve ayar kitabı
section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The individual method of repair is a procedure when parts and units removed from the machine for repair are mounted on the same machine after repair (with the exception of those parts and units which are worn out and have to be replaced by new ones). This method presents the following disadvantages: lengthy idle time, high cost and low quality of repairs. With individual repairs, parts are repaired and manufactured on a separate basis, the machine assembly and adjustment after repair is a difficult and complicated operation and takes a great deal of time and effort; the mechanization of repair is hard to achieve because the design dimensions of machine units and joints are changed; no interchangeability of parts is possible. The individual method of repair is presently used only for huge and nonstandard machines.

product: Tekstil makineleri onarım ve ayar kitabı
section: M e t h o d s o f e l i m i n a t i o n
text: The unit repair method is that at which preliminarily prepared, adjusted, and tested new or repaired units and parts are installed on the machine instead of the removed units and parts. The dismantled parts and units are sent to specialized workshops for processing and repairs. In the case of the unit repair method, the idle time is shorter than at individual repair, the cost of repair is lower and its quality higher. There is no idle time due to the absence of units and parts as the repair and manufacture of parts and units are made in advance and with partial interchange; for mounting the parts and units inconsiderable machine adjustment is required and the repair operations may largely be mechanized.

text: The unit repair method is most efficacious in the case when the equipment is of the same type and when the main units ofthe machines manufactured by different machine-building plants and of differ­ ent models are unified. If the equipment is of different types and its basic units are not unified, the repair method by unit is rendered difficult as a great reserve of different units and parts must be kept Methods and Kinds of Repairs 247 in stock. The parts cannot be interchanged so that a careful adjustment must be carried out. Therefore in these cases the repair method by unit involves only the preparation of requisite units in advance.

text: The in-line unit repair method comprises the restoration, mating and working-in of the most labour-consuming units and mechanisms in workshops equipped with special machines, stands and fixtures. In these special workshops the repairs are carried out in-line, thus ensuring their high efficiency and good quality. The repair teams in this case have only to mount the units on the machines to be repaired and to proceed to their adjustment. The duration of unit repairs that find application in the textile industry may be of one shift and two shifts; and may be carried out on stands and by sections.

Purpose and Structure of the Repair Service in the Textile Enterprises The repair service in textile enterprises operates according to the system of scheduled preventive repairs comprising preventive technical measures, the maintenance and inspection of equipment. Thus, the system of scheduled preventive repairs includes the technic­ al maintenance, current, medium and overhaul repairs of textile machinery. Technical maintenance comprises cleaning and oiling of machines, elimination of small disarrangements, adjustment of units and mechanisms.

text: The duration of periods and cycles between repairs for the equipment in different fields of the textile industry is established depending on the kind of machines and the working conditions. In most cases, at three shift work the periodicity of medium repairs is from 3 to 6 months, and that of overhauls from 2 to 3 years. The repair service at textile enterprises carries out not only the repair of equipment, but also its modernization, erection, manufacture ofnew parts, and the restoration of worn and broken parts, and executes the orders of the maintenance service for keeping the equipment in good working condition.

text: When pressing-in a bush into a gear, a flanged insert of adequate diameter and without interior hole is chosen and is inserted in the aperture of the ribbed stand. Next the gear is placed so as to make its interior hole coincide with the thrust bearing centre. Turning the crank the worm is put in motion and by the intermediate of the thrust bearing it presses in the bushing into the gear. Pressing-out is done in the same way, the only difference being that the flanged insert is chosen with a hole of adequate diameter. This device facilitates the work of turners, reduces the time necessary for the replacement of bearings and protects the hubs from premature wear.

Specifications allow the following run-out of fluted rollers: 0.15 m m for spinning and roving frames and 0.1 m m for drawing frames. The roller shafts of flax spinning frames are made of chromium plated steel and the fluted posts of stainless steel or chromium plated steel. text: Tension rollers are made of tin or carbolite. Tin rollers have a short useful life and their repair requires the use of special devices for unscrewing nuts, reaming of beads, dressing, elimination of indentations on the side face and rim. All these operations are carriedout on a universal stand. In carbolite tension rollers, the roller and shaft ball-bearings are worn-out, the rims are broken and contaminated, and the grease hardens. These rollers are inspected at the time of overhaul and medium repairs of the frame. The rollers are disassembled, washed in straw oil and packed with new grease and the worn*out bearings are replaced. For repairing such rollers the shop must have a mechanized washing unit and also hand presses for press-fitting and pressing-out ball bearings.

In the case of shuttle looms the following units and parts should be repaired in specialized shops: the batteries, dobbies slays, crankshaft with bearings and carriers, the picking motion and reed; in pneumatic looms— the driving box; in rapier looms— the compressors, rapiers and shedding motion; in automatic weft winders— the yarn tension 17* 260 Chapter Seven devices and conveyors; and in sizing machines— the speed variators and reducers, etc. Most of these units are restored at the time of overhaul.

text: When looms are repaired on stands, they are lifted and transported by a special bogie-crane above the equipment and further the loom is transported in the shop on a hand or electric car. The loom is lifted or lowered by a winch or a motor supplied with current from the line or accumulators arranged in the bogie. If the width of the passages is sufficient for driving-out the loom from the row, simple jack bogies are employed which are attached to the frames. The loom is lifted and transported either manually or by an electric car. The equipment is repaired on stands at the time of overhaul which is very time-consuming. The number of stand platforms must suit the number of spare looms.

text: Any assistant foreman knows that the preventive repair is a guarantee of trouble-free machine operation. Proper failure prediction is of great importance. There exist several methods of failure prediction, but they are all aimed at detecting the disarrangements in due time by their outward symptoms. So for instance, let us discuss such a symptom as repeated breakages on the same spindle of a spinning frame. W h e n using the existing method of yarn breakage determination in spinning frames, the repetition of yarn breakages on the same spindles is not registered and the causes of these breakages are not detected. However, this symptom means that some spindles do not properly operate. The existing methods of control must be replaced by control of each spindle at which the technical condition of spinning frames is si­

text: Turning the power ON with the power switch ❶ The power to the sewing machine is placed in the ON state when the "|" mark side of power switch ❶ (1ø 220 - 240V type) is pressed; or in the OFF state when the "0" mark side is pressed. The power to the sewing machine is placed in the ON state when the knob of power switch ❷ (EU type, 1ø 220 - 240V type) is turned by 90 degrees counterclockwise; or in the OFF state when it is turned clockwise to return to its home position. Do not strongly tap the power switch by hand. If the power indicator LED on the panel does not light up after having turned ON the power switch ❶❷ , immediately turn OFF the power switch and check the supply voltage. When you want to re-turn ON power switch ❶❷ after carrying out the aforementioned steps, it is necessary to wait for five minutes or more after you have turned OFF power switch ❶❷ .

text: When you press ❷ after you have changed the function setting number, the set value of the relevant function setting number is displayed. Change the set value by pressing ❸ and Confirm the set value by pressing ❷ . If you have changed the set value during sewing, there is a parameter that enable the set value when you depress the back part of the pedal. section: ① Stop position setting (Function setting No. P02)
text: This function setting number is used for setting the stop position of the needle. P02 0: The needle stops at its upper position 1: The needle stops at its lower position 2: The needle stop position is not specified The needle stop position can also be changed with the relevant button on the operation panel. The upper stop position and the lower stop position can be selected alternately by pressing ❺ . When the display B dot lights up, the needle stops at its upper position. When the display B dot goes out, the needle stops at its lower position. In the case the function setting number "P02" is set to "2: The needle stop position is not specified" under the function setting mode, the needle stop position is not specified regardless of ON / OFF of the display B dot.

section: I M P O RTA NT S A F E G U A R D S
text: To reduce the risk of fire, electric shock and/or injury to persons, basic safety precautions should always be followed when using electrical appliances, including the following: READ ALL INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE USING THE COFFEEMAKER. Do not touch the coffeemaker's hot surfaces. Use handles or knobs. To protect against electric shock, do not immerse the power cord, power plug or coffeemaker in water or in any other liquid. Close adult supervision is necessary when this appliance is used by or near children. Turn the coffeemaker OFF and unplug the power cord from the power source when the coffeemaker and clock are not in use and before cleaning. Allow the coffeemaker parts to cool before putting on or taking off parts and before cleaning the appliance.

text: Do not operate any appliance with a damaged power cord or power plug, or operate it after the appliance malfunctions, or has been damaged in any manner. Do not let the power cord hang over edge of table or counter, or allow it to come into contact with hot surfaces. Do not place this coffeemaker on or near a hot gas stove or electric burner or in a heated oven. To disconnect the coffeemaker, turn it OFF, then remove the power plug from the power supply. Place the appliance on a hard, flat level surface to avoid interruption of airflow underneath the coffeemaker. Avoid contact with any moving parts. This coffeemaker is designed for household use only.

text: Su disco de filtración de agua necesita reemplazarse cada mes (aproximadamente cada 30 ciclos de colado). Si la máquina no se utilizará durante un período extendido, enjuague el filtro de agua con agua limpia y limpie la cafetera.

text: El agua dura puede dejar una mancha blancuzca en la jarra, y el café y el té pueden hacer que esta mancha se torne marrón. Para eliminar las manchas en la jarra: Llene la jarra con una solución compuesta de partes iguales de agua y vinagre y déjela reposar en la jarra por aproximadamente 20 minutos. Descarte la solución, y luego lave y enjuague la jarra. No utilice limpiadores fuertes abrasivos que puedan rasguñar la jarra, los rasguños pueden hacer que la jarra se quiebre. Circule el remanente de la solución limpiadora a través de la cafetera. Descarte la solución limpiadora y enjuague bien la jarra con agua limpia. Llene el tanque de agua con agua fresca y limpia. Coloque la jarra vacía de vuelta en la cafetera, centrada en el plato calefactor.

section: CLEAN YOUR COFFEEMAKER BEFORE USING THE FIRST TIME
text: Make sure your first cup of coffee is as good as can be by cleaning your MR. COFFEE ® Coffeemaker before its first use. Just follow these simple steps: Wash the decanter, decanter lid and the filter basket in a mixture of mild detergent and water. Rinse each thoroughly (please refer to the parts diagram listed above). Replace all the parts and close the lid. Then, run a brew cycle with water only, without adding coffee and coffee filter. When brewing is complete, turn your coffeemaker off, discard the water in the decanter and rinse the decanter, decanter lid, and filter basket. Your coffeemaker is now ready to use. Enjoy it!

section: Limpieza Diaria de su Cafetera MR. COFFEE ®
text: Siempre desenchufe la cafetera y permita que se enfríe antes de limpiarla. Saque la canasta del filtro, el filtro permanente (no está incluido con todos los modelos), la cubierta de la regadera (rotándola en contra de las manecillas del reloj), la jarra y la tapa de la jarra y lávelos en una solución de agua caliente y detergente líquido suave. Nunca utilice polvos limpiadores, fibras metálicas o cualquier otro material abrasivo. La jarra de vidrio y su tapa, la canasta de colar, el filtro permanente y la regadera de acero inoxidable sí se pueden lavar en el escurridor superior del lavaplatos, pero no así el disco del filtro de agua. ¡ADVERTENCIA! Nunca sumerja la cafetera en sí en agua ni en ningún otro líquido, ni la ponga en el lavaplatos.

El limpiador MR. COFFEE ® está disponible en muchas tiendas de ventas detallistas o llamando al Departamento de Servicios al Consumidor de MR. COFFEE ® al 1800-MR COFFEE (1-800-672-6333).

section: To Set the Delay Brew Time:
text: While the display is on the clock mode, simply press the SET DELAY button (Figure 3) and, while the DELAY BREW yellow light is flashing, set the brew time by pressing the HOUR and MINUTE buttons (Figure 4). section: Para Programar la Hora del Reloj:
text: Enchufe el cordel eléctrico en un tomacorriente estándar. El reloj parpadeará en el panel de controles para indicar que la hora aún no ha sido programada. Oprima y mantenga oprimidos los botones de HOUR (HORA) y MINUTE (MINUTO) hasta que el reloj marque la hora actual. Los indicadores de AM o PM se encenderán en la parte superior de la pantalla (Figuras 1 y 2). ¡El reloj ya ha sido programado! ADVERTENCIA: El oprimir cualquier botón antes de programar el reloj hará que el reloj comience a marcar la hora a partir de las 12:00 a.m. Usted debe programar el reloj si desea usar la característica de Demora del Colado.

section: INSTRUCCIONES ESPECIALES SOBRE EL CORDEL ELÉCTRICO
text: Se provee un cordel eléctrico corto para disminuir los riesgos de que una persona o mascota se pudieran enredar o tropezar con un cordel más largo. Se puede adquirir y utilizar una extensión eléctrica si se usa con precaución. Si se utiliza una extensión eléctrica, la calificación eléctrica rotulada de la extensión debe ser de al menos 10 amperios y 120 voltios. El cordel extendido resultante debe acomodarse para que no cuelgue del borde de un mostrador o mesa donde pueda ser tirado por niños o donde se pueda tropezar con él accidentalmente.

text: Esta unidad cuenta con un enchufe polarizado (uno de sus contactos es más ancho que el otro). Para disminuir el riesgo de una descarga eléctrica, este enchufe sólo podrá penetrar en un tomacorriente polarizado. Si el enchufe no penetra completamente en el tomacorriente, inviértalo. Si aún no se puede enchufar, comuníquese con un electricista autorizado. No modifique el enchufe de manera alguna. Usted puede ajustar el largo del cordel eléctrico de manera que sea de la longitud precisa que usted desee. Para aumentar el largo del cordel eléctrico: agarre el cordel eléctrico (no el enchufe) y hálelo hacia arriba de su hendidura con delicadeza, retirándolo de la cafetera. Para disminuir el largo del cordel eléctrico: agarre el cordel eléctrico (no el enchufe) y hálelo hacia arriba de su hendidura, insertándolo con delicadeza en la cafetera. Fije el cordel en la hendidura cuando termine.

Se requiere supervisión adulta atenta cuando esta unidad sea utilizada por, o cerca de, niños. Apague la cafetera (oprima "OFF" [APAGAR]) y desenchufe el cordel eléctrico del tomacorriente cuando no se esté utilizando la cafetera o el reloj, y antes de limpiarlos. text: Grounded tools must be plugged into an outlet properly installed and grounded in accordance with all codes and ordinances. Never remove the grounding prong or modify the plug in any way. Do not use any adaptor plugs. Check with a qualified electrician if you are in doubt as to whether the outlet is properly grounded. If the tools should electrically malfunction or break down, grounding provides a low resistance path to carry electricity away from the user. Improper grounding can shock, burn, or electrocute. Grounded tools are equipped with threeconductor cord and three-prong type plugs. Before plugging in the tool, be certain the outlet voltage supplied is within the voltage marked on the nameplate. Do not use "AC only" rated tools with a DC power supply.

section: ATTACHING THE SWITCH TO THE TABLETOP (Fig. 3)
text: Assembly Hint: It may be easier to attach the switch bracket if you stand the tabletop on its back edge for this step. 1.Align the two holes in the switch mounting bracket (15) with the two through-holes in the router tabletop. From the top side of the table, insert two #10-32 x 1 1 /2″ pan-head machine screws (34) through the tabletop and bracket and secure the bracket in place with two small washers (30) and two #10-32 KEPS nuts (29) (Fig. 3). Insert two #10-32 KEPS nuts (29) into the hex-shaped recesses in the back of the switch assembly (14) with the toothed washer facing away from the recess. Secure the switch to the switch mounting bracket with two #10-32 x 1/2″ pan-head machine screws (33) while holding the KEPS nuts in place in the recess with your finger.

The switch has an internal, resettable circuit breaker to provide overload protection.

section: ATTACHING AND USING A WET/DRY VACUUM
text: MAKE SURE THE SWITCH IS OFF AND UNPLUGGED BEFORE PLUGGING IN A WET/DRY VACUUM OR REACHING IN THE AREA UNDER THE TABLE OR NEAR THE ROUTER BIT! This router table features two vacuum ports for the attachment of a wet/dry vac with a 2 1 /2″ nozzle. Select which port will provide optimal results, based on your routing operation: For routing operations where shavings and dust are typically pulled down under the tabletop, such as grooving, use the slotted hole in the back of the table cabinet. This will help prevent a buildup of sawdust and wood chips in the cabinet. To attach, simply push the nozzle into the port. For routing operations where sawdust and wood chips are ejected onto the tabletop, such as many edge-cutting operations, use the vacuum port on the back of the fence. To attach, simply push the nozzle into the port while holding the fence assembly in place.

text: Featherboards are helpful in controlling the workpiece while routing and assist in keeping the workpiece flat on the tabletop. The tabletop featherboard, combined with the fence featherboard, helps keep the workpiece pressed against the fence and tabletop. The best location for the featherboards varies according to your application, workpiece size, and other factors. 1.Loosely install the featherboard(s) as described on page 24. 2.Place the workpiece on the router table so that it is squarely against the fence. 3.Position both featherboards snugly against the workpiece and tighten the clamping knobs. 4.The workpiece should move with some resistance but without requiring a great effort. 5.For wider workpieces, the tabletop featherboard cannot be used. The second featherboard may also be positioned on the fence, if desired.

section: USING THE STARTER PIN FOR EDGE FORMING OF CURVES
text: The starter pin (26) is used instead of the fence for operations that involve routing curves in the workpiece. It should be used only with bits that have pilot bearings. Thread the starter pin into the threaded hole in the mounting plate and tighten securely with a slotted screwdriver (Fig. 32). Attach the starter pin guard (27) to the mounting plate by threading a #10-32 x 3/8″ truss-head machine screw (28) through the hole in the guard post and into the threaded hole in the mounting plate. Align the guard with the hole in the mounting plate so it is over the bit, and securely fasten the guard in place. Always use the starter pin guard when routing with the starter pin. When using the starter pin, the feed direction of the workpiece is always right to left across the front of the bit (Fig. 33). Set the workpiece against the front of the starter pin and swing it slowly into the bit.

Les outils avec mise à la terre sont munis d'un cordon à trois fils et d'une prise à trois fiches. Réglez la hauteur de la garde de sorte qu'elle ne touche pas la fraise de la toupie ou la pièce. La garde permet d'éviter le contact accidentel des mains avec la fraise tournante.

section: Consignes de sécurité supplèmentaires pour la table à toupie
text: Ne placez jamais les doigts près d'une fraise tournante ou sous une garde lorsque la toupie est branchée. Ne tenez jamais la pièce du côté sortie de la fraise. Le fait de pousser la pièce contre le côté sortie de la cloison peut causer le coincement du matériau et un rebond qui pourrait entraîner la main vers la fraise. Servez-vous du guide pour guider l'avance de la pièce. Ne placez pas de matériau entre la fraise de la toupie et le guide pendant que vous découpez le bord de la pièce. Cela causerait le coincement du matériau et un risque de rebond. Les toupies sont conçues pour le travail du bois, des matières semblables au bois, des matières plastiques ou laminées, et non pour couper ou façonner les pièces métalliques. Assurez-vous que la pièce ne contient pas de clou, etc. Le découpage des clous peut entraîner une perte de contrôle.

Dans le cas d'un dysfonctionnement ou d'une décharge disruptive, la mise à la terre assure un trajet de résistance moindre du courant électrique de façon à réduire le risque de choc électrique. text: Les guides biseautés sont très utiles pour contrôler la pièces à toupiller et aident à conserver la pièce à plat sur l'établi. Le guide biseauté de la table, combiné au guide biseauté du guide, aide à conserver la pièce à toupiller pressée contre la garde et la table. Le meilleur emplacement pour les guides biseautés varie selon votre application, la taille de la pièce à toupiller et d'autres facteurs. Installez le guide biseauté sans serrer comme l'indique la page 54. Placez la pièce à toupiller sur la table à toupie de manière à ce qu'elle soit carrément contre la garde. Placez les guides biseautés contre la pièce a toupiller et serrez les boutons de serrage. La pièce à toupiller devrait bouger avec une certaine résistance mais sans nécessiter un grand effort.

section: TOUPILLAGE À L'AIDE DES GUIDES BISEAUTÉS (Fig. 21)
text: Pour des pièces à toupilles plus grandes, vous ne pouvez pas utiliser le guide à languettes de table à toupie. Vous pouvez mettre le second guide à languettes contre la garde, le cas échéant. Vous pouvez acheter d'autres guides biseautés modèle RA1187 chez votre détaillant Bosch. Les guides biseautés sont des auxiliaires pour aider à maintenir la pièce à travailler en position lors du toupillage sur une table à toupie. Ils ne sont PAS conçus pour tenir à elles seules la pièce à travailler lorsque celle-ci entre en contact avec la fraise ou à tout autre moment lorsque la fraise tourne. Ne lâchez JAMAIS la pièce à travailler pendant le toupillage lorsque vous utilisez un guide biseauté avant que la coupe soit terminée et que la pièce à travailler soit complètement dégagée de la fraise.

section: UTILISATION DE LA GOUPILLE DE DÉMARRAGE POUR LA FORMATION DES BORDS DE COURBE
text: La goupille de démarrage (26) est utilisée au lieu de la cloison pour les opérations qui nécessitent la taille des profils courbes de la pièce. Elle doit être utilisée seulement avec les fraises qui possèdent des paliers pilotes. Vissez la goupille de démarrage dans le trou taraudé de la plaque de montage et fixez solidement à l'aide d'un tournevis pour écrou à fente (Fig. 32). Attacher le protecteur (27) de la goupille de démarrage à la plaque de montage en vissant une vis à métaux à tête bombée n°10-32 x 3/8 po (28) dans le trou du montant du protecteur et dans le trou filetée de la plaque de montage. Alignez le protecteur au trou de la plaque de montage de manière à ce qu'il soit au dessus de la fraise et fixez solidement le protecteur en place. Utilisez toujours le protecteur de la goupille de démarrage pour toupiller avec la goupille de démarrage.

section: Normas de seguridad para herramientas mecánicas
text: Lea y entienda el manual de se fresador y estas instrucciones. El incumplimiento de todas las instrucciones indicadas a continuación puede dar lugar a lesionespersonales graves.

text: Mantenga el área de trabajo limpia y bien iluminada. Las mesas desordenadas y las áreas oscuras invitan a que se produzcan accidentes. No utilice herramientas mecánicas en atmósferas explosivas, tales como las existentes en presencia de líquidos, gases o polvos inflamables. Las herramientas mecánicas generan chispas y éstas pueden dar lugar a la ignición del polvo o los vapores. Mantenga a las personas que se encuentren presentes, a los niños y a los visitantes alejados al utilizar una herramienta mecánica. Las distracciones pueden hacer que usted pierda el control.

text: Las herramientas con conexión a tierra deben enchufarse en un tomacorriente instalado y conectado a tierra adecuadamente de acuerdo con todos los códigos y ordenanzas. Nunca quite el terminal de conexión a tierra ni modifique el enchufe de ninguna forma. No utilice enchufes adaptadores. Consulte a un electricista calificado si tiene dudas sobre si el tomacorriente está conectado a tierra adecuadamente. En caso de que las herramientas tengan algún funcionamiento defectuoso o avería de tipo eléctrico, la conexión a tierra proporciona una ruta de resistencia baja para transportar la electricidad alejándola del usuario. La conexión incorrecta a tierra puede causar sacudidas eléctricas, quemar o electrocutar. Las herramientas con conexión a tierra están equipadas con un cordón de tres conductores y enchufes del tipo de tres terminales.

text: Las herramientas con aislamiento doble están equipadas con un enchufe polarizado (un terminal es más ancho que el otro). Este enchufe entrará en un tomacorriente polarizado solamente de una manera. Si el enchufe no entra por completo en el tomacorriente, déle la vuelta. Si sigue sin entrar, póngase en contacto con un electricista competente para instalar un tomacorriente polarizado. No haga ningún tipo de cambio en el enchufe. El aislamiento doble elimina la necesidad del sistema de cordón de energía de tres hilos conectado a tierra y la fuente de energía conectada a tierra. text: Evite el contacto del cuerpo con las superficies conectadas a tierra tales como tuberías, radiadores, estufas de cocina y refrigeradores. Hay mayor riesgo de que se produzcan sacudidas eléctricas si su cuerpo está conectado a tierra. Si la utilización de la herramienta mecánica en lugares húmedos es inevitable, se debe usar un interruptor de circuito para fallos a tierra para suministrar la energía a la herramienta. Los guantes de goma para electricista y el calzado antideslizante aumentarán más la seguridad personal. No exponga las herramientas mecánicas a la lluvia ni a situaciones húmedas. La entrada de agua en una herramienta mecánica aumentará el riesgo de que se produzcan sacudidas eléctricas.

text: Si es necesario un cable de extensión, se debe usar uno con conductores de tamaño adecuado que sea capaz de transportar la corriente necesaria para la herramienta. Esto evitará caídas de tensión excesivas, pérdida de potencia o el recalentamiento. Las herramientas conectadas a tierra deben usar cables de extensión de 3 hilos que tengan enchufes de 3 terminales y receptáculos para 3 terminales. NOTA: Cuanto más pequeño es el número de calibre, más es el cable.

section: CÓMO ENSAMBLAR LOS LADOS A LA PARTE TRASERA (Fig. 1)
text: NOTA: Los orificios de montaje para los paneles izquierdos y derechos se encuentran espaciados de manera tal que el panel sólo pueda ajustarse al lado correcto de la parte trasera. En cada panel, la superficie que posee orificios embutidos siempre debe estar orientada hacia AFUERA. 1.Sosteniendo el panel trasero (6) en forma derecha, con la entrada del cable a la izquierda (ver Fig. 1), sujete el panel izquierdo (4) al panel trasero mediante dos tornillos de conexión de cabeza Allen (38). 2.Sujete el panel derecho (5) al panel trasero mediante dos tornillos de conexión de cabeza Allen (38). 3.Ajuste todas las fijaciones firmemente con la llave hexagonal de 4 mm (43). La cabeza del tornillo va a sobresalir un poco de la superficie del panel. NO LO AJUSTE DE MÁS.

text: Consejo de ensamblado: la instalación del soporte de montaje puede resultarle más fácil si para este paso deposita la mesa sobre su parte trasera. 1.Alinee los dos orificios del soporte de montaje (15) con los dos orificios de la superficie de la mesa fresadora. Desde el lado superior de la mesa, inserte dos tornillos de máquina #10-32 x 1 1 /2″ (34) a través de la superficie de la mesa y el soporte, y asegure este último en su lugar mediante dos tuercas KEPS #10-32 (29) (Fig. 3). Inserte dos tuercas KEPS #10-32 (29) en los orificios de forma hexagonal de la parte trasera de la ensembladura del interruptor (14) con la arandela dentada orientada hacia afuera de la muesca. Asegure el interruptor al soporte de montaje mediante dos tornillos de máquina de cabeza segmental #10-32 x 1/2″ (33) mientras sostiene las tuercas KEPS en su lugar con sus dedos.

section: CÓMO SUJETAR LA SUPERFICIE DE LAMESA (Fig. 4)
text: NOTA: La guía del inglete de aluminio puede estar preinstalados en la superficie de la mesa. Retirarla para acceso a los orificios de montaje. 1.Con el ensamblado de la base en posición derecha, coloque la superficie de la mesa (1) sobre ésta, y asegúrese de que el interruptor esté en la parte delantera de la mesa (Fig. 4). 2.Sujete la superficie de la mesa a la base mediante cuatro tornillos de conexión de cabeza Allen (38). 3.Ajuste todas las fijaciones firmemente con la llave hexagonal de 4mm. La cabeza del tornillo debe estar debajo de la superficie de la mesa. NO LO AJUSTE DE MÁS.

En cada tornillo, ajuste con una pequeña arandela (30) y una tuerca KEPS #10-32 (29).

section: CÓMO UNIR Y USAR UNA ASPIRADORA DE SECADO/MOJADO
text: ¡CERCIÓRESE DE QUE EL INTERRUPTOR ESTÉ APAGADO Y DESCONECTADO ANTES DE CONECTAR UNAASPIRADORA DE SECADO/ MOJADO O ACERCARSE AL ÁREA POR DEBAJO DE LAMESA O CERCA DE LA BROCA DE FRESADO! La mesa de fresado cuenta con dos puertos de vacío para conectar una aspiradora de mojado/secado con una boquilla de 2 1 /2″. Elija el puerto que le brinde mejores resultados, basándose en las operaciones de fresado: Para las operaciones de fresado en las que comúnmente se acumulan recortes de madera y aserrín debajo de la superficie de la mesa - como en el ranurado- utilice el orificio ranurado de la parte trasera del gabinete de la mesa. Esto servirá para prevenir una acumulación de aserrín y astillas de madera en el gabinete. Para conectar, simplemente inserte la boquilla en el puerto.

section: CÓMO UNIR Y USAR UNA ASPIRADORA DE SECADO/MOJADO
text: Para operaciones de fresado en las que el aserrín y las astillas de madera saltan a la superficie de la mesa -como en las operaciones de corte de bordesutilice el puerto de vacío ubicado en la parte posterior de la guía. Para conectar, simplemente inserte la boquilla en el puerto mientras sostiene el ensamblado de la guía en su lugar. La aspiradora puede conectarse al interruptor de la mesa de fresado, y el cable puede colocarse a través de la ranura del puerto de vacío ubicado en la parte trasera del gabinete. Asegúrese de que el cable no interfiera con las operaciones de fresado. Operar la mesa de fresado sin una aspiradora de secado/ mojado puede resultar en una acumulación excesiva de aserrín y astillas de madera debajo de la ensambladura de la guía y dispositivo de protección superior, y en el gabinete, reduciendo el desempeño de la mesa de fresado y la ensambladura de la guía.

section: CÓMO INSTALAR LA BROCA DE LA FRESADORA (CORTADOR)
text: Siempre cerciórese de que la fresadora esté APAGADA y el cable eléctrico esté DESCONECTADO antes de hacer cualquier ajuste. Instale la broca de fresado según las instrucciones que se incluyen con la fresadora. Dada la gran variación de las brocas de la fresadora, es posible que ciertas brocas no operen siempre de la forma deseada con esta mesa de fresado. Para asegurar que la mayoría de las brocas comunes tengan un desempeño satisfactorio, instale la broca de manera que el portabrocas de la fresadora encaje 3/4″ de la espiga de la broca de fresado. Si la espiga de la broca de fresado se sale del portabrocas, retroceda la broca de la fresadora aproximadamente 1/16″ para permitir apretarla correctamente. NUNCA INSTALE BROCAS DE FRESADO CON MENOS DE 3/4″ DE ENCAJE DE LA ESPIGA EN EL PORTABROCAS.

section: CÓMO FRESAR UTILIZANDO TABLAS DE BISELADO (FIG. 21)
text: Las tablas de biselado son de utilidad para controlar la pieza de trabajo mientras se realiza el trabajo de fresado, y sirven para mantener la pieza de trabajo plana sobre la mesa. La tabla de biselado de la superficie de la mesa, en combinación con la tabla de biselado de la guía ayuda a mantener la pieza de trabajo presionada contra la guía y la superficie de la mesa. La mejor ubicación para las tablas de biselado varía según la aplicación, el tamaño de la pieza de trabajo y otros factores. 1.Sin apretar, instale la(s) tabla(s) de biselado(s) según se describe en la página 86. 2.Coloque la pieza de trabajo en la mesa de fresado de manera que quede cuadrada contra la guía. 3.Coloque ambas tablas de biselado cómodamente contra la pieza de trabajo y apriete las perillas abrazaderas. 4.La pieza de trabajo se debe mover con cierta resistencia pero sin necesidad de un gran esfuerzo.

section: CÓMO AJUSTAR EL REFRENTADO DE LA GUÍA (FIG. 22)
text: Las caras derecha e izquierda de la guía se encuentran sujetas a la cara frontal de la guía de la mesa fresadora, y se las puede ajustar hacia adentro o hacia fuera desde la broca de la fresadora a fin de permitir espacios adecuados para brocas de distintos tamaños. Para obtener la mejor sujeción durante las operaciones de fresado, los refrentados de la guía deben ubicarse lo más cerca posible de la broca, sin llegar a entrar en contacto con la misma (normalemente ca. 1/4″ de la broca). 1.Afloje las dos perillas de sujeción en la parte posterior del refrentado de la guía y coloque las caras hacia adentro o hacia fuera desde la broca de la fresadora, según sea necesario. section: USO DE LA PATA DE ARRANQUE PARA FORMAR LOS BORDES DE LAS CURVAS
text: La pata de arranque (26) se utiliza en vez de la guía para las operaciones que involucran el fresado de curvas en la pieza de trabajo. Se debe usar únicamente con brocas que tienen cojinetes de piloto. Enrosque el pasador de arranque en el orificio enroscado en la placa de montaje y apriete firmemente con un destornillador ranurado (Fig. 32). Una el protector de la pata de arranque (27) a la placa de montaje enroscando un tornillo (28) de máquina de cabeza segmental #10-32 x 3/8″ a través del orificio en el poste de protección hacia al orificio enroscado en la placa de montaje. Alinee el dispositivo de seguridad con el orificio en la placa de montaje de manera que quede encima de la broca y firmemente sujete el dispositivo de seguridad en su lugar. Siempre utilice el protector de seguridad de la pata de arranque al fresar con la pata de arranque.

section: USO DE LA PATA DE ARRANQUE PARA FORMAR LOS BORDES DE LAS CURVAS
text: Cuando utilice la pata de arranque, la dirección de alimentación de la pieza de trabajo es siempre de derecha a izquierda por el frente de la broca (Fig. 33). Fije la pieza de trabajo contra el frente de la pata de arranque y balancéelo lentamente hacia la broca. Mientras esté fresando, cerciórese de que la pieza de trabajo esté siempre en contacto con el cojinete piloto de la broca. Se debe utilizar el protector de seguridad auxiliar para este tipo de operación. Mantenga los dedos alejados de la broca giratoria. No intente fresar piezas de trabajo pequeñas.

section: CÓMO UTILIZAR UN CALIBRADOR DE INGLETE (NO INCLUIDO)
text: La ranura de calibración de inglete en T de aluminio puede utilizarse en la gran mayoría de las ranuras de inglete de sierra de mesa fija que miden 3/4″ de ancho x 3/8″ de profundidad. NOTA: Para TODAS las operaciones de fresado que requieran el uso del calibrador del inglete con la guía, ASEGÚRESE de alinear la guía con la ranura del calibrador del inglete de la mesa fresadora antes de realizar cualquier tipo de corte. Los ingletes pueden cortarse si se desajusta la perilla de la cabeza del transportador, se gira la cabeza del transportador a 60° en cualquier dirección y se vuelve a ajustar la perilla.

Los ingletes pueden cortarse si se desajusta la perilla de la cabeza del transportador, se gira la cabeza del transportador a 60° en cualquier dirección y se vuelve a ajustar la perilla.
